definition_zh: 地质学家；地质工作者；研究岩层与地球历史的人
definition_en: a scientist who studies rocks, layers, minerals and the long history of the earth, often by fieldwork as well as laboratory analysis
core_image: 一个人蹲在岩壁前，手举地质锤敲下一块带层理的岩石
scene: 这里指「地质学家」。 The geologist read the cliff like a page, naming each layer in order.
sceneCN: 这里 geologist 是「地质学家」的本义（第 1 个义项：以岩层为研究对象的人）；句意：这位地质学家像读一页书那样读那道崖壁，依次说出每一层。图中可辨识物件：地质锤、放大镜、岩层剖面、记录本、安全帽。

pos.zh: 地质学家；地质工作者（可数名词，复数形式规则变化）

senses.title: A scientist of rocks and strata
senses.titleCN: 岩石与地层的研究者：本义
senses.definition: a scientist whose subject is the solid earth, its rocks, minerals and layered history
senses.definitionCN: 以固体地球、岩石、矿物与层状历史为研究对象的科学家
senses.example: A geologist can date the flow of lava from its mineral grains.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家能根据矿物颗粒测定熔岩流出的年代。
senses.why: geology joins Greek gē 'earth' and -logia 'study, account'; -ist marks the person, so a geologist is literally 'one who studies the earth'.
senses.whyCN: geology 由希腊 gē“大地”与 -logia“研究、论述”构成，-ist 标记从事者，因此 geologist 字面就是“研究大地的人”。

senses.title: The field worker
senses.titleCN: 野外地质工作者：在山野里读岩的人
senses.definition: one who maps and samples rock exposures outdoors rather than only in a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 在野外测绘、采样岩石露头，而非只在实验室工作的人
senses.example: The geologist spent the summer mapping exposures along the fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地质工作者整个夏天都在测绘断层沿线出露的岩体。
senses.why: Because strata are visible only where they break the surface, the profession's core skill has always been reading outcrops in the field.
senses.whyCN: 由于地层只有在出露地表处才可见，这门职业的核心技能始终是在野外读露头。

senses.title: The exploration specialist
senses.titleCN: 资源勘探地质师：找矿找油的人
senses.definition: an applied geologist who locates oil, gas, groundwater or ore for industry
senses.definitionCN: 为工业寻找石油、天然气、地下水或矿石的应用型地质工作者
senses.example: The company hired a geologist to assess the shale under the plain.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘请了一位地质师评估平原下方的页岩。
senses.why: Industry needs predictions about what lies underground, and that is exactly the stratigraphic reading a geologist supplies.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要关于地下埋藏什么的预测，而这正是地质学家所提供的层序判读。

senses.title: The planetary geologist
senses.titleCN: 行星地质学家：读别的星球表面
senses.definition: a geologist who applies earthly rock science to the surfaces of the moon, Mars or other bodies
senses.definitionCN: 把地球岩石科学用于月球、火星等天体表面的地质学家
senses.example: A planetary geologist compared the crater floors on Mars with basalt fields on earth.
senses.exampleCN: 一位行星地质学家把火星的坑底与地球的玄武岩区作比较。
senses.why: The same processes of impact, flow and erosion leave records elsewhere, so the earth-trained eye transfers to other worlds.
senses.whyCN: 撞击、流动与侵蚀等同一批过程在其他天体也留下记录，因此受训于地球的眼光可转移到别的世界。

senses.title: The engineering geologist
senses.titleCN: 工程地质人员：为建筑判断地基
senses.definition: a geologist who judges ground conditions for tunnels, dams, foundations and slopes
senses.definitionCN: 为隧道、水坝、地基与边坡判断地下条件的地质工作者
senses.example: An engineering geologist warned that the slope would fail after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 一位工程地质人员警告说，大雨之后该边坡会失稳。
senses.why: Buildings rest on materials a geologist can name and test, so the discipline becomes a safety service at construction sites.
senses.whyCN: 建筑坐落在能由地质工作者命名并测试的材料上，于是这门学问在工地变成一项安全服务。

senses.title: The hazard assessor
senses.titleCN: 灾害评估者：判读地震与滑坡风险
senses.definition: one who studies faults, volcanoes and unstable ground to estimate future risk
senses.definitionCN: 研究断层、火山与不稳定地面以估计未来风险的人
senses.example: The geologist mapped old landslide scars before the town expanded.
senses.exampleCN: 在小镇扩建之前，这位地质学家测绘了旧滑坡的痕迹。
senses.why: Past rock movement is written into the landscape; reading it forward into future risk is the hazard branch of the same skill.
senses.whyCN: 过去的岩体运动被写入地貌；把这种记录向前读成未来风险，就是同一技能的风险分支。

senses.title: The map-maker of strata
senses.titleCN: 地层编图者：把岩层画成图
senses.definition: one who compiles geological maps showing the age and arrangement of rock units
senses.definitionCN: 编制显示岩层年代与分布关系的地质图的人
senses.example: The geologist finished a sheet covering four hundred square kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地质学家完成了一幅覆盖四百平方公里的图幅。
senses.why: A geological map is the profession's written form: the geologist converts scattered outcrops into a continuous picture of what lies beneath.
senses.whyCN: 地质图是这门职业的书面形态：地质学家把零散露头转成一幅连续的地下图景。

senses.title: The teacher and explainer
senses.titleCN: 教学与科普者：把深时讲给人听
senses.definition: a geologist who teaches the subject or explains deep time to the public
senses.definitionCN: 教授这门学科或向公众解释深远年代的地质工作者
senses.example: The geologist showed visitors how a river cuts through a million years in one bank.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地质学家向参观者展示一条河如何在一道岸壁上切开百万年。
senses.why: Deep time is invisible without explanation, so part of the role is turning rock evidence into a story nonspecialists can follow.
senses.whyCN: 深时若不经解释便不可见，因此这一角色的一部分工作就是把岩石证据转成非专业者能跟上的一段叙述。

intro.en: Geologist is geolog(y) plus -ist. The compound is Greek in its parts, Latin in its transmission, and modern in its meaning. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geologist 是 geolog(y) 加 -ist。其构件属希腊语，传承经拉丁语，词义则是近代形成的。年代为约数。

items.en: gē meant 'earth', and logos meant 'word, account, reason'. The compound geologia would have meant 'an account of the earth'; it is not common in surviving classical texts.
items.cn: gē 意为“大地”，logos 意为“言说、记述、道理”。复合形式 geologia 本应意为“关于大地的论述”，在现存古典文本中并不常见。

items.en: The Latinized form geologia appears in the 17th century for the study of the earth's materials. Several writers used it independently, so no single coiner can be named with certainty.
items.cn: 拉丁化形式 geologia 于 17 世纪出现，指对地球物质的研究。多位作者各自使用过它，因此无法确定唯一的创制者。

items.en: Only in the late 18th and early 19th centuries did geology settle on its modern meaning: the study of strata and earth history, with field mapping as its method.
items.cn: 直到 18 世纪末至 19 世纪初，geology 才固定为现代含义：研究地层与地球历史，以野外填图为方法。

items.en: -ist comes from Greek -istēs through Latin -ista and French -iste, and names a person engaged in something. Geologist is recorded from the late 18th century.
items.cn: -ist 经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste 来自希腊 -istēs，指从事某事的人。geologist 的记录可追溯到 18 世纪后期。

items.en: The 20th century split the role into branches such as petroleum geologist, engineering geologist and planetary geologist.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个角色分化为石油地质师、工程地质人员、行星地质学家等分支。

items.en: The first use of geologia and of geologist is uncertain, and the deeper sense of Greek logos ranges from 'word' to 'reason', so the original force of the compound is disputed.
items.cn: geologia 与 geologist 的首见年代存疑；希腊 logos 的深层含义从“言词”到“道理”不等，因此该复合词最初的含义有争议。

note.en: The first group contains words built on the same stems; the second contains other earth-science specialists who study different materials.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干构成的词；第二组是研究不同对象的其他地球科学专家。

entries.definition: The discipline itself, or the rock structure of a region. A geologist practises geology.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科本身或某地的地质构造；地质学家从事的是这门学科。

entries.definition: Relating to geology, as in geological map or geological time. It cannot stand for a person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，如地质图、地质年代；不能用来指人。

entries.definition: An obsolete variant for a geologist, formed with -er instead of -ist. It appears only in older texts.
entries.definitionCN: 地质学家的废弃变体，以 -er 而非 -ist 构成，仅见于旧文本。

entries.definition: A specialist in the description of places, climate and distribution, from -graphy 'write'; a geologist reads strata, a geographer maps surfaces and peoples.
entries.definitionCN: 专长于描述地点、气候与分布，源自 -graphy“书写”；地质学家读地层，地理学家绘地表与人群。

entries.definition: Anyone studying the planet, including oceans, atmosphere and magnetism; a geologist is one member of this wider group.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球的任何人，包括海洋、大气与地磁；地质学家是这一更大群体中的一个分支。

entries.definition: One who studies the chemistry and structure of minerals rather than whole rock sequences.
entries.definitionCN: 研究矿物的化学成分与结构，而非整套岩层序列的人。

entries.definition: One who records and interprets seismic waves; a geologist may study faults, but a seismologist measures the shaking itself.
entries.definitionCN: 记录并解释地震波的人；地质学家可以研究断层，但地震学家测量的是震动本身。

entries.definition: One who specializes in volcanic systems and eruptions, a narrower branch of geology.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻火山系统与喷发的人，是地质学中更窄的分支。

entries.definition: A person who searches for ore or gold, often by practical experience rather than formal geological training.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找矿石或黄金的人，常凭实践经验而非正规地质训练。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: geo- 'earth' + -logy 'study' + -ist 'person': the person who studies the earth.
normal.cn: geo-“大地”+ -logy“研究”+ -ist“人”：研究大地的人。

normal.en: geology is the field, geologist is the person, geological is the adjective; keep the trio straight.
normal.cn: geology 是学科，geologist 是人，geological 是形容词；三者要分清。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: field geologist, petroleum geologist, planetary geologist, engineering geologist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：野外地质工作者、石油地质师、行星地质学家、工程地质人员。

normal.en: A geologist's basic tools are the hammer, the hand lens and the notebook.
normal.cn: 地质工作者的基本工具是地质锤、放大镜和记录本。

normal.en: Do not confuse geologist with geographer: rocks versus places.
normal.cn: 别把 geologist 与 geographer 混淆：一个是岩石，一个是地点。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff face as a stack of pages, each layer a sentence written in sand and shell.
abstract.cn: 想象崖壁是一叠书页，每一层都是用沙与贝壳写下的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer tapping a stone and a clock hand jumping back a million years with each blow.
abstract.cn: 想象锤子敲一下石头，时钟的指针就回跳一百万年。

abstract.en: Picture scattered outcrops joined by faint lines into one continuous underground sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象零散露头被细线连成一整幅连续的地下图纸。

examples.en: The geologist sampled the ash layer on both sides of the valley to compare the two sections.
examples.cn: 这位地质学家在谷地两侧都采了火山灰层样品，以对比两个剖面。

examples.en: After the earthquake, a geologist measured how far the fence had been offset.
examples.cn: 地震之后，一位地质学家测量了栅栏被错开的距离。

examples.en: The museum's geologist explains to school groups why the fossils are older than the lava above them.
examples.cn: 博物馆的地质学家向学生团体解释，为什么化石比覆盖其上的熔岩更古老。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地（geo）质学家爱敲石头（logist 像‘逻辑师’）”——读岩层如读书 → geologist 地质学家

root: 希腊 gē“大地”+ logos“言说、道理”→ geologia“关于大地的论述”；拉丁 geologia + -ist（从事者后缀）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses belong to one figure: a person who reads stone. The same reader moves from outcrop to industry, to other planets, to risk, to maps and to the classroom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都属于同一个人物：读石头的人。这同一个读石者从露头走向工业、走向别的星球、走向风险、走向地图，最后走向课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kneeling figure tapping a layered cliff with a hammer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个蹲在层状崖壁前、用锤子敲击的人。

branches.en: THE READER: the scientist and the field worker are the same core role seen in the library and on the cliff.
branches.cn: 读石者：学科专家与野外工作者是同一核心角色在书房与崖壁上的两种样子。

branches.en: RESOURCES: reading strata becomes a service to mining, oil and water supply.
branches.cn: 资源：读地层变成对采矿、石油与供水的服务。

branches.en: OTHER GROUND: the same eye is turned to other planets and to the ground under a dam.
branches.cn: 别处的地面：同一双眼睛转向别的行星，也转向水坝之下的土地。

branches.en: RISK AND RECORD: old movement becomes future hazard, and scattered evidence becomes a published map.
branches.cn: 风险与记录：过去的运动变成未来的风险，零散证据变成公开发表的地图。

branches.en: THE EXPLAINER: the geologist also converts deep time into words the public can hold.
branches.cn: 解释者：地质学家还负责把深时转换成公众能把握的语言。

intro.en: Geologist is a clean three-part word: geo- 'earth', -log- 'study or account', -ist 'person'. The middle element is the same one that gives logic and dialogue.
intro.cn: geologist 是清晰的三段式词：geo-“大地”、-log-“研究或论述”、-ist“人”。中间这一段也构成 logic 与 dialogue。

latinIntro.en: Greek logos supplied a whole family through Latin and French: logic, dialogue, biology, geology, theology, psychology and technology all carry -logy or -logue.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 logos 经拉丁与法语衍生出整族词：logic、dialogue、biology、geology、theology、psychology、technology 都带 -logy 或 -logue。

items.meaning: a person who studies the earth's rocks
items.example: The geologist logged the section in a waterproof notebook.
items.exampleCN: 这位地质学家在防水本上记录了该剖面。

items.meaning: the science of the earth's solid materials
items.meaningCN: 研究地球固体物质的科学
items.example: The geology of the basin is dominated by sandstone.
items.exampleCN: 该盆地的地质以砂岩为主。

items.meaning: relating to rock structure and earth history
items.meaningCN: 与岩层构造和地球历史有关的
items.example: The survey produced a new geological map.
items.exampleCN: 这次调查绘制了新的地质图。

items.example: Geologic time is measured in millions of years.
items.exampleCN: 地质年代以百万年计。

items.meaning: the chemistry of rocks and fluids
items.meaningCN: 岩石与流体的化学研究
items.example: Geochemistry can reveal where the granite came from.
items.exampleCN: 地球化学能揭示花岗岩的来源。

items.meaning: the physics of the earth's interior and fields
items.meaningCN: 研究地球内部与场的物理学
items.example: Geophysics locates the ore body without digging.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理学不必开挖就能定位矿体。

items.meaning: the study of living things; shows -logy at work
items.meaningCN: 研究生物的科学；展示 -logy 的构词方式
items.example: Biology and geology meet in the study of fossils.
items.exampleCN: 生物学与地质学在化石研究中相遇。

items.meaning: the study of valid reasoning, from the same logos
items.meaningCN: 研究有效推理的学问，同出 logos
items.example: The argument's logic is sound even if its data are thin.
items.exampleCN: 即便数据单薄，这个论证的逻辑仍然成立。

latinEntries.meaning: a word, an account, or reasoned explanation
an account of the earth (early modern Latin)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 关于大地的论述（早期近代拉丁）

definition_en: in a way that belongs to the essential nature of something
core_image: 一块木头内部的纹理，从表面看不见却贯穿整块材料
scene: 果核里的苦味来自它本身的结构，与烹饪方式无关。 The bitterness of the kernel is inherently chemical, not a matter of cooking.
sceneCN: 这里指由自身构造决定的性质（第 1 个义项：修饰形容词，指本质属性）；句意为果核的苦味本质上来自化学构造，与烹饪方式无关。

pos.zh: 内在地；本质上；固有地

senses.title: By its own nature
senses.definition: in a way that belongs to the essential nature of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 以属于某物本质的方式
senses.example: The material is inherently brittle at low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料在低温下本身就很脆。
senses.why: Modifying an adjective, it says the property comes from what the thing is, not from how it is used.
senses.whyCN: 修饰形容词时，它说明这一性质来自事物本身，而不是来自它的用法。

senses.title: Not by circumstance
senses.definition: used to contrast an internal cause with external conditions
senses.definitionCN: 用来把内部原因与外部条件形成对照
senses.example: The conflict was inherently structural rather than personal.
senses.exampleCN: 这场冲突本质上是结构性的，而不是个人恩怨。
senses.why: The word shifts the explanation from situation to design, and the contrast with rather than is typical.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把解释从处境移到构造上，与「而不是」搭配的对照很典型。

senses.title: Inherently linked
senses.definition: used of two things whose connection cannot be separated
senses.definitionCN: 用于两者之间无法分离的联系
senses.example: Freedom of speech is inherently linked to responsibility.
senses.exampleCN: 言论自由与责任天然相连。
senses.why: In this fixed pattern the adverb marks an inseparable relation, close to by definition.
senses.whyCN: 在这一固定搭配里，副词标记不可分离的关系，接近「按定义就是如此」。

senses.title: No system is inherently safe
senses.definition: used with a negative to deny that a property is guaranteed by the thing alone
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，否认某一性质仅凭事物本身就能保证
senses.example: No encryption method is inherently secure against every attack.
senses.exampleCN: 没有哪种加密方法本身就足以抵御一切攻击。
senses.why: Under negation the word attacks a naive assumption: the thing may become safe, but not by nature alone.
senses.whyCN: 在否定句中它针对一种天真假设：事物可以变安全，但不是单靠本性。

senses.title: Inherently more stable
senses.titleCN: 比较句中的结构性优势
senses.definition: used before a comparative to claim that an advantage comes from design
senses.definitionCN: 放在比较级前，主张优势来自结构本身
senses.example: The arched form is inherently more stable than a flat one.
senses.exampleCN: 拱形结构本身就比平直结构更稳定。
senses.why: With a comparative, the word argues that the difference is built into the structure, not added later.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，它主张差别已写进结构中，而不是后来附加的。

senses.title: Inherently ambiguous
senses.titleCN: 技术与学术中的固有难题
senses.definition: in technical or academic prose, marking a difficulty that cannot be engineered away
senses.definitionCN: 在技术或学术散文中，标记无法靠工程手段消除的困难
senses.example: Translation is inherently ambiguous when two languages divide the world differently.
senses.exampleCN: 当两种语言对世界的划分不同时，翻译本身就有歧义。
senses.why: The register presents the difficulty as a property of the task, which limits what any method can promise.
senses.whyCN: 这一语域把困难说成任务本身的属性，从而限制任何方法能承诺的范围。

senses.title: Inherently valuable
senses.definition: used in ethics to say that value belongs to a thing, not to its usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 在伦理讨论中指价值属于事物本身，而不属于它的用处
senses.example: The forest is inherently valuable, not merely a store of timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林本身就有价值，不只是木材的储备。
senses.why: Ethical writing uses the word to separate worth in itself from instrumental worth.
senses.whyCN: 伦理写作借它把「自身的价值」与「作为工具的价值」分开。

senses.title: Inherently limited
senses.definition: used of a capacity that cannot exceed what the design allows
senses.definitionCN: 用于无法超出设计所允许范围的能力
senses.example: Human memory is inherently limited in the number of items it can hold.
senses.exampleCN: 人的记忆在能容纳的条目数量上本身就有上限。
senses.why: The word describes a ceiling set by the nature of the system, often with a hint of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述由系统本性设定的上限，常带一点无奈的接受。

intro.en: Inherently comes from the Latin verb for sticking fast inside, through its participle and adjective, plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「牢牢粘在内部」的动词，经分词与形容词，再加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb haerere means to stick, cling or be fixed in place.
items.cn: 动词意为「粘住、附着、固定在某处」。

items.en: The prefix in-, meaning in, plus haerere gives inhaerere, to stick fast inside something.
items.cn: 表示「在内」的前缀与「粘住」合成「牢牢附着于某物之内」。

items.en: The present participle inhaerens, sticking in, becomes the source of the adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词意为「附着于内的」，成为形容词的来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin inheren(t)- supplies the adjective stem used in philosophy and law.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语提供哲学与法学使用的形容词词干。

items.en: English inherent appears in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十六世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix and spreads into technical and ethical argument.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀，并扩展到技术与伦理讨论。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin sticking-root, including words built with other prefixes; the second group contrasts inherent belonging with value or quality viewed in itself.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「粘附」词根，包括带其他前缀的同族词；第二组对照「固有属性」与「就本身而言」的价值或性质。

entries.definition: To exist as a permanent quality in something.
entries.definitionCN: 作为恒久性质存在于某物之中。

entries.definition: The state of existing as part of a thing's nature.
entries.definitionCN: 作为事物本性的一部分而存在的状态。

entries.definition: Sticking to a surface or to a person or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于表面，或追随某人、某项事业。

entries.definition: Sticking together logically; consistent and clear.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑上彼此粘合；连贯而清晰。

entries.definition: In itself, considered apart from its use or setting; the emphasis falls on the thing viewed alone.
entries.definitionCN: 就本身而言，撇开用途与处境；重心在单独看待该事物。

entries.definition: From birth or from the earliest nature, often of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来地，多用于生物。

entries.definition: Because of the character a thing or person has.
entries.definitionCN: 由于事物或人本身的性格、特性。

entries.definition: At the deepest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 在最深层、最基础层面上。

entries.definition: In its essential respects, when everything secondary is set aside.
entries.definitionCN: 就本质方面而言，撇开一切次要因素。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real sticking-root and the real patterns of blame, negation and technical limits.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「粘附」词根，以及归因、否定与技术限度中的真实搭配。

normal.en: The root means to stick fast, so an inherent quality is glued into the thing and cannot be peeled off.
normal.cn: 词根意为「牢牢粘住」，所以固有属性是粘进事物内部、揭不下来的。

normal.en: With rather than it moves the explanation away from people and situations.
normal.cn: 与「而不是」连用时，它把解释从人和处境上移开。

normal.en: No system is inherently safe is a warning, not a compliment.
normal.cn: 「没有系统本身就安全」是一句警告，不是称赞。

normal.en: Before a comparative it says the advantage was designed in, not added on.
normal.cn: 放在比较级前，它说优势是设计进去的，不是后加的。

normal.en: Ethics uses it to say a thing matters for what it is, not for what it sells.
normal.cn: 伦理学用它说明某物因其本身而重要，而不是因其售价。

abstract.en: An inherent property is the grain in the wood that no surface polish can change.
abstract.cn: 固有属性就是木头里的纹理，表面打磨改变不了它。

abstract.en: Blaming a design instead of a person is a way of saying the outcome was already inside the plan.
abstract.cn: 把责任归于设计而非个人，等于说结果早已藏在方案里。

abstract.en: To call a limit inherent is to stop promising that more effort will remove it.
abstract.cn: 把限度说成固有，就是不再承诺更多努力能把它消除。

examples.en: The task is inherently social, since it cannot be done without others.
examples.cn: 这项任务本质上是社会性的，因为没有他人就无法完成。

examples.en: Some risk is inherently attached to every surgical procedure.
examples.cn: 每台手术都固有地带有一定风险。

examples.en: The method is inherently slow but extremely accurate.
examples.cn: 这种方法本身很慢，却极为精确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因黑然特利」——黑在材料内部的性质，从里面长出来

root: 拉丁语动词「粘住」加表示「在内」的前缀，构成「牢牢附着于内」的分词与形容词；英语借入形容词后加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate essential nature, contrast with circumstance, inseparable linking, negated guarantees, structural comparison, built-in difficulty, value in itself, and design-imposed limits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理本质属性、与外部条件的对照、不可分离的联系、被否定的保证、结构性比较、固有难题、自身价值，以及设计带来的限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the grain inside a block of wood, invisible on the surface but running through the whole material.
core.cn: 核心意象：木块内部的纹理，表面看不见却贯穿整块材料。

branches.en: THE NATURE: a property that comes from what the thing is.
branches.cn: 本性：来自事物之所以为该物的性质。

branches.en: THE INNER CAUSE: the explanation lies in design, not circumstance.
branches.cn: 内部原因：解释落在构造上，而非处境上。

branches.en: THE GLUE: a connection that cannot be separated.
branches.cn: 粘合：无法分离的联系。

branches.en: THE DENIED GUARANTEE AND THE BUILT-IN EDGE: what nature does not promise, and what it does provide.
branches.cn: 被否认的保证与内置优势：本性不承诺什么，又确实提供什么。

branches.en: THE UNAVOIDABLE SHAPE: difficulty, value and limits that belong to the thing itself.
branches.cn: 无法回避的形态：属于事物本身的困难、价值与限度。

intro.en: Inherently is a Latin in-prefix, a Latin sticking-root and participle ending, plus an English adverb suffix. The same root also builds coherent and adherent.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「在内」前缀、「粘附」词根与分词词尾，再加英语副词后缀构成；同一词根还构成「连贯的」与「附着的」。

latinIntro.en: The root haerere is about clinging; the prefix decides whether the clinging is inward, together or toward something.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「粘住」；前缀决定这种粘附是向内、彼此相合，还是朝向某物。

items.example: The prefix locates the sticking inside the thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「粘附」定位在事物内部。

items.example: The verb gives the physical image of glue.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「胶水粘住」的具体意象。

items.example: The compound verb makes the attachment internal.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把这种附着变成内部的。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into a description of a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成对事物的描述。

items.example: The participle supplies the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供形容词词干。

items.example: A different prefix gives the English word adherent.
items.exampleCN: 换一个前缀就得到英语的「附着的」。

items.example: The same root with a together-prefix gives coherent.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根配上「共同」前缀，得到「连贯的」。

items.example: The suffix turns inherent into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The noun names the state that the adverb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名副词所描述的状态。

definition_zh: 色素沉着；着色；色素分布
definition_en: the presence, amount or deposition of pigment in a tissue or material, or the colouring that results
core_image: 皮肤表层下一簇深色颗粒均匀铺开，像撒了一层细沙
scene: 海边正午，一名渔民的肩膀被晒成深褐色。 Sun exposure increases pigmentation in the skin, forming freckles and dark patches.
sceneCN: 这里 pigmentation 指「皮肤中色素增多而形成的着色」（第 1 个义项：日晒后黑色素在皮肤中沉积，使肤色变深）；句意为日晒使皮肤色素沉着增加，形成雀斑与深色斑块。图中可辨识物件：晒成深褐色的肩膀、肩带留下的浅色痕、帽檐阴影。

pos.zh: 色素沉着；着色；色素分布（不可数）

senses.title: Colouring from pigment in the skin
senses.titleCN: 皮肤中色素形成的着色
senses.definition: the deposition of pigment in skin that produces a tan, freckles or naturally dark complexion
senses.definitionCN: 色素在皮肤中沉积，形成晒黑、雀斑或天生深肤色
senses.example: Sun exposure increases pigmentation in the skin, forming freckles and dark patches.
senses.exampleCN: 日晒使皮肤色素沉着增加，形成雀斑与深色斑块。
senses.why: The -ation noun names the process and its visible result: pigment has settled into tissue and changed its colour.
senses.whyCN: -ation 名词同时命名过程与可见结果：色素沉入组织并改变了它的颜色。

senses.title: Medical disorder of pigment
senses.definition: an abnormal increase, decrease or distribution of pigment that signals a skin condition
senses.definitionCN: 色素的异常增多、减少或分布，提示某种皮肤病变
senses.example: The clinic treats pigmentation caused by old sun damage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所治疗旧日晒伤留下的色素沉着。
senses.why: Once pigmentation is measured, any departure from the expected amount becomes a clinical finding.
senses.whyCN: 一旦色素量可被测量，任何偏离预期的量都成了临床所见。

senses.title: Colour in plant tissue
senses.definition: the presence of coloured compounds such as anthocyanins in leaves, petals or fruit
senses.definitionCN: 叶片、花瓣或果实中存在花青素等着色化合物
senses.example: Cool nights deepen the pigmentation of the maple leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷的夜晚加深了枫叶的色素。
senses.why: Plants produce their own pigments, so the same noun covers tissue colour without any animal skin.
senses.whyCN: 植物自己产生色素，因此这个名词无需动物皮肤也能指组织颜色。

senses.title: Colour pattern in feathers or fur
senses.titleCN: 羽毛或毛皮的颜色分布
senses.definition: the arrangement of pigment in feathers, hair or fur that gives an animal its markings
senses.definitionCN: 羽毛、毛发或毛皮中色素的分布，形成动物的斑纹
senses.example: The owl's pigmentation breaks up its outline against the trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 这只猫头鹰的羽色把它的轮廓从树干背景中打散。
senses.why: Feathers and fur are dead tissue coloured by pigment, exactly the surface the noun describes.
senses.whyCN: 羽毛与毛皮是由色素着色的死组织，正是这个名词所描述的表面。

senses.title: Pigment in the eye
senses.definition: the amount of melanin in the iris or retina that determines eye colour and light tolerance
senses.definitionCN: 虹膜或视网膜中黑色素的含量，决定眼睛颜色与耐光程度
senses.example: Low pigmentation in the iris lets more light scatter, so the eyes look blue.
senses.exampleCN: 虹膜色素少会让更多光线散射，于是眼睛看起来是蓝色。
senses.why: The eye is another pigmented surface; the noun needs no new meaning for it.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛是又一个带色素的表面，这个名词无需新义就能覆盖。

senses.title: Colour of microbial colonies
senses.definition: the pigment produced by bacteria or fungi that colours their colonies
senses.definitionCN: 细菌或真菌产生、使菌落显色的色素
senses.example: The plate showed pigmentation typical of a soil bacterium.
senses.exampleCN: 培养皿显示出一种土壤细菌典型的色素。
senses.why: Colour is a by-product of microbial chemistry, so the noun applies to colonies exactly as it does to skin.
senses.whyCN: 颜色是微生物化学的副产物，因此这个名词用于菌落与用于皮肤完全同理。

senses.title: Industrial colouring of materials
senses.definition: the addition of pigment to plastics, coatings or ceramics to give them colour
senses.definitionCN: 向塑料、涂料或陶瓷加入色素以赋予颜色
senses.example: Uniform pigmentation is essential in automotive paint.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车漆中均匀的着色至关重要。
senses.why: Industry applies pigment to inert materials, extending the biological noun to manufacture.
senses.whyCN: 工业把色素施加到惰性材料上，把这个生物名词扩展到制造领域。

senses.title: Pigment traces in fossils
senses.definition: chemical residues of pigment preserved in fossils that reveal original colours
senses.definitionCN: 化石中保存的色素化学残留，可揭示原本的颜色
senses.example: Pigmentation preserved in the fossil shows the dinosaur was dark-backed.
senses.exampleCN: 化石中保存的色素表明这只恐龙背部颜色深。
senses.why: Deep time leaves only the pigment chemistry, but it is still the same noun: colour preserved in stone.
senses.whyCN: 深时只留下色素的化学成分，但仍是同一个名词：保存在石头里的颜色。

intro.en: Pigmentation is Latin pigmentum 'paint' plus -ation, from the verb pigmentare; pigmentum itself comes from pingere 'to paint'. The word entered English through French in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: pigmentation 由拉丁 pigmentum「颜料」加 -ation 构成，出自动词 pigmentare；pigmentum 本身来自 pingere「绘画」。这个词 19 世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Pingere 'to paint, to embroider' is the verb at the base of the family; its past participle is pictus.
items.cn: pingere「绘画、刺绣」是该词族底层的动词，其过去分词为 pictus。

items.en: Pigmentum meant 'colouring matter, paint' and was formed from pingere with the noun suffix -mentum.
items.cn: pigmentum 意为「着色物、颜料」，由 pingere 加名词后缀 -mentum 构成。

items.en: French pigmentation named the action of colouring and reached English in the 1830s, first in medical descriptions.
items.cn: 法语 pigmentation 命名着色行为，1830 年代进入英语，最初用于医学描述。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology applied the noun to skin, feathers and plant tissue, fixing the modern sense.
items.cn: 19 世纪生物学把这个名词用于皮肤、羽毛与植物组织，固定了现代义。

items.en: The deeper source of pingere is reconstructed as a root meaning 'to cut, mark, paint'; the form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: pingere 的更早来源被重构为表示「切、刻、画」的词根；该形式是重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and root): the 1830s date is approximate, and the reconstructed root of pingere has competing proposals. The Latin pigmentum layer itself is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：1830 年代为约数，pingere 的重构词根存在不同提案；拉丁 pigmentum 这一层本身可靠。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same Latin family that are easily confused; group two holds words for colour change that differ in cause or in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族中容易混淆的形式；第二组是表示颜色变化的词，区别在成因或范围。

entries.definition: The colouring matter itself; pigmentation is its presence or deposition in tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指着色物质本身；pigmentation 指它在组织中的存在或沉积。

entries.definition: Having pigment; it describes a thing, not the process that put pigment there.
entries.definitionCN: 指含有色素的；描述事物，而非把色素放进去的过程。

entries.definition: Relating to pigment, as in pigmentary layer; it does not name the colouring itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表示与色素有关的，如色素层；并不命名着色本身。

entries.definition: The loss of pigment, the reverse of pigmentation; the prefix de- reverses the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 指色素丧失，与 pigmentation 方向相反；前缀 de- 表示反向。

entries.definition: The overall colour pattern, whatever produces it; pigmentation names the pigment cause specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体色彩图案，不问成因；pigmentation 特指色素这一成因。

entries.definition: The skin's darkening after sun exposure; pigmentation is the underlying deposit, tanning the everyday result.
entries.definitionCN: 指日晒后皮肤变深；pigmentation 是底层的沉积，tanning 是日常可见的结果。

entries.definition: A change of colour seen as damage or fault; pigmentation is neutral about whether the colour is wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 指被视为损伤或缺陷的颜色变化；pigmentation 不判断这种颜色是否受欢迎。

entries.definition: Colour left on a surface by an external substance; pigmentation usually arises inside the tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指外部物质在表面留下的颜色；pigmentation 多由组织内部产生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin chain of pingere, pigmentum and -ation, the real medical compounds, and the fixed collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：pingere、pigmentum 与 -ation 的真实拉丁链条、真实的医学复合词，以及固定搭配。

normal.en: pingere 'paint' gives pigmentum 'paint', and -ation names the result.
normal.cn: pingere「画」给出 pigmentum「颜料」，-ation 命名结果。

normal.en: The family runs pigment, pigmented, pigmentary, pigmentation, depigmentation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pigment、pigmented、pigmentary、pigmentation、depigmentation。

normal.en: Medical pairs: hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation.
normal.cn: 医学配对：色素沉着过度与色素减少。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: skin pigmentation, pigmentation disorder, facial pigmentation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 skin pigmentation、pigmentation disorder、facial pigmentation。

normal.en: The word covers skin, feathers, leaves, eyes, colonies and paint.
normal.cn: 这个词覆盖皮肤、羽毛、叶片、眼睛、菌落与涂料。

abstract.en: Picture fine dark grains settling under a sheet of skin like sand under glass.
abstract.cn: 想象细小的深色颗粒沉在皮肤之下，像玻璃下的沙。

abstract.en: Picture a maple leaf deepening its red as the nights get cold.
abstract.cn: 想象一片枫叶随着夜寒加深而变红。

abstract.en: Picture an eye whose blue is only scattered light over very little pigment.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蓝眼睛，那蓝色只是极少色素之上散射的光。

examples.en: Pigmentation varies with latitude and with inherited melanin levels.
examples.cn: 色素沉着随纬度与遗传的黑色素水平而变化。

examples.en: The fungus produces pigmentation only when exposed to light.
examples.cn: 这种真菌只在见光时产生色素。

examples.en: The paint's pigmentation faded after a decade in the sun.
examples.cn: 这种漆的着色在日晒十年后褪去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pigment（色素）+ -ation（状态）」——色素落下来形成的状态 → 色素沉着；着色

root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画」→ 拉丁 pigmentum「颜料」→ 法语 pigmentation → 英语 pigmentation；pingere 的更深词根为重构形式，存在不同提案。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow pigment as it settles: into skin, into a disorder, into plants, feathers, eyes, colonies, industrial coatings and finally fossil stone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟随色素沉降的路径：进入皮肤、成为病变、进入植物、羽毛、眼睛、菌落、工业涂层，最后进入化石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fine dark grains settling under a sheet of skin like sand beneath glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：细小深色颗粒沉在皮肤之下，像玻璃下的沙。

branches.en: HUMAN BODY: skin and iris colour record how much pigment sits where.
branches.cn: 人体：皮肤与虹膜颜色记录色素沉积的位置与数量。

branches.en: MEDICINE: excess or loss of pigment becomes a diagnosis.
branches.cn: 医学：色素过多或过少成为诊断。

branches.en: OTHER ORGANISMS: plants, feathers and microbes each colour their own tissue.
branches.cn: 其他生物：植物、羽毛与微生物各自给组织上色。

branches.en: INDUSTRY: pigment is added to inert materials by design.
branches.cn: 工业：色素被有意加入惰性材料。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: pigment residues survive in fossils.
branches.cn: 深时：色素残留能在化石中保存。

intro.en: Pigmentation is a Latin noun stem plus -ation; pigmentum in turn is pingere plus -mentum, so two Latin suffixes stack in the history of the word.
intro.cn: pigmentation 是拉丁名词词干加 -ation；pigmentum 又是 pingere 加 -mentum，因此这个词的历史上叠了两个拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin pingere, pigmentum and pictus supply the paint family behind pigmentation and picture alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pingere、pigmentum 与 pictus 提供「颜料」词族，pigmentation 与 picture 都出自这里。

items.example: The pigment is ground fine before mixing.
items.exampleCN: 颜料在混合前被磨得很细。

items.example: The ending names the deposit and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名沉积及其结果。

items.example: Skin pigmentation increased after the holiday.
items.exampleCN: 假期后皮肤色素沉着增加了。

items.example: The lesion is unevenly pigmented.
items.exampleCN: 这块病灶的色素分布不均。

items.example: A pigmentary layer lies beneath the retina.
items.exampleCN: 视网膜下有一层色素层。

items.example: Pigment cells cluster in the iris.
items.exampleCN: 色素细胞聚集在虹膜中。

items.example: Each pigment granule holds melanin.
items.exampleCN: 每个色素颗粒都装着黑色素。

definition_zh: 多山的；山区的；如山一般巨大的；艰巨的
definition_en: having many mountains; also enormously large, like a mountain, or extremely difficult
core_image: 一片地面上接连不断的山脊，几乎没有一块平坦的空地
scene: 车队沿着盘山公路缓慢爬升，两侧的坡壁一次次逼近车窗。 The mountainous terrain makes every kilometre slow.
sceneCN: 此处指「地形以山地为主、坡多而少平地」（第 1 个义项：大片地面被山体占据）；句意为这种多山的地形让每一公里都走得很慢。图中可辨识物件：盘山公路、逼近车窗的坡壁、连续的山脊、缓慢行驶的车队。

pos.zh: 多山的；山区的；如山一般巨大的；艰巨的

senses.title: Full of mountains
senses.definition: used of a region whose surface is mostly high, steep land
senses.definitionCN: 用于地面大部分为高而陡的陆地的地区
senses.example: The north of the country is mountainous and thinly populated.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的北部多山，人口稀少。
senses.why: -ous means 'full of' or 'having the character of', so mountainous is literally 'mountain-full'.
senses.whyCN: -ous 表示「充满」或「具有……的性质」，所以这个词字面就是「装满了山的」。

senses.title: Belonging to mountain life
senses.titleCN: 山区的；山地生活特有的
senses.definition: typical of mountain areas, their climate, roads or communities
senses.definitionCN: 具有山区特征的，如气候、道路或社区
senses.example: Mountainous villages often depend on a single road.
senses.exampleCN: 山区的村庄往往只依赖一条公路。
senses.why: Once a region is called mountainous, everything in it can share the label as a setting.
senses.whyCN: 一片地区一旦被称为多山，其中的一切都可以作为「场景」共用这个标签。

senses.title: As tall as a mountain, of waves
senses.definition: used of waves or water that rise to a great height
senses.definitionCN: 用于升得极高的波浪或水体
senses.example: Mountainous waves broke over the harbour wall.
senses.exampleCN: 如山的巨浪越过港口防波堤。
senses.why: Height is the shared feature: the water takes the profile of a peak without being made of rock.
senses.whyCN: 共同点是高度：水面取得了山峰的轮廓，尽管它不是岩石构成的。

senses.title: Enormous in amount
senses.definition: used of debts, costs or numbers that are huge and hard to reduce
senses.definitionCN: 用于巨大而难以削减的债务、成本或数字
senses.example: Mountainous debt forced the company to sell its factories.
senses.exampleCN: 庞大的债务迫使公司卖掉工厂。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from visible terrain to quantity: what is large enough to block the view becomes mountainous.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从可见地形转向数量：大到挡住视线的东西，就被说成如山一般。

senses.title: Huge and solid in form
senses.definition: used of an object that is enormously tall or bulky
senses.definitionCN: 用于极其高大或庞大的物体
senses.example: A mountainous iceberg drifted into the shipping lane.
senses.exampleCN: 一座巨大的冰山漂进了航道。
senses.why: Shape alone is enough: a mass with steep sides reads as mountainous even when it is ice, not rock.
senses.whyCN: 仅凭形状就够了：侧面陡峭的巨块即使由冰而非岩石构成，读起来也像山。

senses.title: Extremely difficult, like a climb
senses.definition: used of a task that is very hard and takes a long effort
senses.definitionCN: 用于非常艰难、需要长期努力的任务
senses.example: Reforming the tax system was a mountainous task.
senses.exampleCN: 改革税制是一项艰巨的任务。
senses.why: If a mountain is a great obstacle, then an obstacle of mountain size is mountainous in difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 如果山是巨大的障碍，那么有山那么大难度的障碍就是「如山般艰巨」的。

senses.title: Of mountainous relief, in geography
senses.definition: a technical description of terrain dominated by high relief
senses.definitionCN: 对以高起伏地形为主的地貌的技术描述
senses.example: Mountainous relief covers about a third of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 山地地貌约占这个省的三分之一。
senses.why: Geography uses the adjective for a measurable class of terrain, not for a single peak.
senses.whyCN: 地理学把这个形容词用于一类可测量的地形，而不是指单独一座峰。

senses.title: Huge in bodily form
senses.definition: a literary or informal use for a very large person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 文学作品或口语中形容十分高大的人或动物
senses.example: A mountainous figure filled the doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 一个硕大的身影堵住了门口。
senses.why: The same size metaphor now applies to a body: bulk that fills a space is read as terrain.
senses.whyCN: 同一个尺度比喻现在用到了身体上：占满空间的体量被读成地形。

intro.en: Mountainous is an English derivative of mountain plus the Latin suffix -ous. Its first recorded use is early modern, and the dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mountainous 是英语由 mountain 加拉丁后缀 -ous 构成的派生词，最早书证见于近代早期，年代为约数。

items.en: Latin -osus meant 'full of, abounding in', as in montuosus 'mountainous' and formosus 'shapely'.
items.cn: 拉丁 -osus 表示「充满、富于」，如 montuosus「多山的」与 formosus「形状美好的」。

items.en: Old French -ous, from Latin -osus, became the productive adjective ending that English borrowed with many Romance words.
items.cn: 古法语 -ous 来自拉丁 -osus，成为英语随大量罗曼语词借入的能产形容词词尾。

items.en: English already had mountaine as a noun; the adjective was formed on the English noun with the borrowed suffix rather than taken whole from Latin.
items.cn: 英语此时已有名词 mountaine；形容词是在英语名词上附加借来的后缀构成，而非整词借自拉丁语。

items.en: The written adjective is recorded from the sixteenth century, first describing terrain and later extending to huge waves and large amounts.
items.cn: 该形容词的书证见于 16 世纪，最初描写地形，后来扩展到巨浪与大量事物。

items.en: The senses 'huge in amount' and 'extremely difficult' are later figurative extensions built on the visible height of a mountain.
items.cn: 「数量庞大」与「极其艰巨」两个义项是后来的比喻延伸，建立在山可见的高度之上。

note.en: The first group holds words built on or beside mountain; the second holds adjectives for steep, high terrain.
note.cn: 第一组是与 mountain 同族或形近的词；第二组是表示陡峭高地的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun that mountainous is built on; it names the thing, while the adjective describes a place full of it.
entries.definitionCN: mountainous 所依附的名词；它指山本身，而形容词描述充满山的地区。

entries.definition: The adverb form, describing how something is shaped or how large it is; it is not a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，描述某物的形状或规模；并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for the mountain zone of a region, built directly on Latin montanus; mountainous describes the whole area, montane names a belt.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由拉丁 montanus 构成的技术形容词，指某一地区的山地地带；mountainous 描述整片地区，montane 命名一条地带。

entries.definition: A person who climbs mountains; it shares the mountain stem but names an agent, not a landscape.
entries.definitionCN: 登山者；共享 mountain 词干，但指人，不指地貌。

entries.definition: Having many hills rather than mountains; the slopes are lower and rounder, so hilly is milder than mountainous.
entries.definitionCN: 有许多小丘而非高山；坡更低更圆，因此 hilly 比 mountainous 温和。

entries.definition: Belonging to the zone above the tree line, or to the Alps by name; it stresses altitude and ecology, not the mere presence of mountains.
entries.definitionCN: 指树线以上的高山区，或专指阿尔卑斯山；强调海拔与生态，而不只是有山。

entries.definition: Describing rough, uneven terrain; it stresses texture and difficulty of passage rather than height.
entries.definitionCN: 形容崎岖不平的地形；强调表面的粗糙与通行困难，而非高度。

entries.definition: Extremely tall, used of peaks, buildings or people; it describes height from the viewer's angle, not a whole region.
entries.definitionCN: 极高的，用于山峰、建筑或人；从观看者角度描述高度，不指整片地区。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix -ous, the real base noun and the fixed phrases that separate terrain from metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀 -ous、真实的基础名词，以及区分地形义与比喻义的固定搭配。

normal.en: mountain + -ous 'full of': a place full of mountains.
normal.cn: mountain + -ous「充满」：装满了山的地区。

normal.en: The suffix is Latin -osus, also seen in dangerous, famous and spacious.
normal.cn: 这个后缀是拉丁 -osus，也见于 dangerous、famous 与 spacious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mountainous region, mountainous terrain, mountainous waves.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 mountainous region、mountainous terrain、mountainous waves。

normal.en: The base noun keeps the concrete sense; the adjective can move to debt, tasks and bodies.
normal.cn: 基础名词保留具体义；形容词则可以移到债务、任务与身体上。

normal.en: Compare montane: mountainous describes the whole region, montane names the high belt inside it.
normal.cn: 对比 montane：mountainous 描述整片地区，montane 命名其中的高山地带。

abstract.en: Picture a map where flat green shrinks until almost every cell is brown ridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，平坦的绿色不断缩小，直到几乎每一格都是褐色的山脊。

abstract.en: Picture a wave photographed from a low boat so that it fills the frame like a cliff.
abstract.cn: 想象从低矮的小船上拍摄一道浪，它像悬崖一样占满画面。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of bills so high that it hides the person behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠账单高到把后面的人完全挡住。

examples.en: The mountainous border region is crossed by only two paved roads.
examples.cn: 这片多山的边境地区只有两条铺装公路穿过。

examples.en: Mountainous seas forced the ferry to stay in port.
examples.cn: 如山的海况迫使渡轮留在港内。

examples.en: The project became a mountainous effort once the old pipes were exposed.
examples.cn: 旧管道一暴露出来，这项工程就变成了一项艰巨的大工程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「毛（mao）+ 天（tain）+ 乐死（ous）」—— 毛茸茸的山顶顶到天，看得人乐坏了 → 多山的

root: mountain + -ous（拉丁 -osus「充满……的」）→ 字面「充满山的」；mountain 源自拉丁 mons、montis。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from a landscape full of peaks, then lend that height to waves, debts, objects, tasks, terrain classes and bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「遍地是山的地区」出发，再把这种高度借给波浪、债务、物体、任务、地形类别与身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface with almost no flat ground left between ridge after ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片地面上，山脊一道接一道，几乎不剩平地。

branches.en: THE LAND ITSELF: ordinary description and technical terrain classification.
branches.cn: 土地本身：日常描述与技术性的地形分类。

branches.en: LIFE IN THAT LAND: climate, roads and villages take the label as their setting.
branches.cn: 那片土地上的生活：气候、道路与村庄把这个标签当作自身场景。

branches.en: HEIGHT WITHOUT ROCK: waves and icebergs borrow the profile of a peak.
branches.cn: 没有岩石的高度：巨浪与冰山借用山峰的轮廓。

branches.en: SCALE AS BURDEN: huge amounts and hard tasks become mountains you must move.
branches.cn: 规模即负担：庞大数量与艰难任务变成必须搬动的山。

branches.en: THE BODY AS TERRAIN: a bulk that fills a doorway is read like a slope.
branches.cn: 身体即地形：堵住门口的巨大体量被读成一面坡。

intro.en: The adjective is transparent: a native-borrowed noun plus a Latin suffix that means 'full of'.
intro.cn: 这个形容词的构造一目了然：一个借入的名词加上表示「充满」的拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin -osus produced Old French -ous, the ending English uses in numerous adjectives of abundance or character.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -osus 产生古法语 -ous，英语用它构成大量表示「富于」或「具有某种性质」的形容词。
