senses.title: A finite procedure for a problem
senses.definition: a set of steps that always ends and always yields an answer for the allowed inputs
senses.definitionCN: 对允许的输入总能终止并给出答案的一组步骤
senses.example: The manual gives an algorithm for checking every receipt twice.
senses.exampleCN: 手册给出了一套把每张收据核对两遍的算法。
senses.why: the word began as the name of a written calculating method, so its core sense is a method laid out step by step rather than a single trick.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一种写下来的计算方法，核心义因此是按步骤铺开的方法，而不是某个单点窍门。

senses.title: A procedure precise enough for a computer
senses.titleCN: 精确到可交给计算机执行的步骤
senses.definition: a procedure stated so exactly that a machine can carry it out without guessing
senses.definitionCN: 表述得足够精确，机器无需猜测即可执行的步骤
senses.example: The algorithm must say what to do at every branch, not just at the start.
senses.exampleCN: 算法必须说明每个分支该做什么，而不只是开头怎么做。
senses.why: computers removed every human gap in the procedure, so the modern sense stresses total explicitness.
senses.whyCN: 计算机抹掉了步骤中一切由人填补的空隙，现代词义因此强调完全的明确性。

senses.title: The method as an object of study
senses.definition: the abstract object whose running time and memory use can be measured and compared
senses.definitionCN: 可以测量并比较运行时间与内存占用的抽象对象
senses.example: Two algorithm designs can give the same answers at very different costs.
senses.exampleCN: 两种算法设计可以给出相同答案，代价却差得很远。
senses.why: once procedures were written formally, they could be analysed like mathematical objects, and the noun named that object.
senses.whyCN: 步骤一旦被形式化地写出，就能像数学对象一样被分析，名词便指这个对象。

senses.title: A named routine in software
senses.definition: a standard procedure such as sorting or searching, often named after its strategy
senses.definitionCN: 排序、搜索等标准步骤，常按其所用策略命名
senses.example: The sort algorithm merges small lists before joining them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个排序算法先把小列表合并，再把它们接起来。
senses.why: libraries of reusable procedures needed names, and each named procedure was called an algorithm after its method.
senses.whyCN: 可复用的过程库需要名字，每个具名过程依其方法被称为一个算法。

senses.title: A rule set for calculation
senses.definition: a fixed set of rules for performing arithmetic with written numerals
senses.definitionCN: 用写出的数字进行算术运算的固定规则集
senses.example: The medieval algorithm for long division spread with Arabic numerals.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的长除法算法随阿拉伯数字一起传播。
senses.why: the oldest sense is simply the rules of decimal calculation that the word's namesake taught, and this sense survives in the older spelling algorism.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思就是这个词的同名者所教的十进制计算规则，这一义保存在较早拼写 algorism 里。

senses.title: A decision procedure in logic
senses.definition: a mechanical method that decides, in finitely many steps, whether a statement follows from given rules
senses.definitionCN: 在有限步内判定某陈述是否可由给定规则推出的机械方法
senses.example: No algorithm decides every question in that formal system.
senses.exampleCN: 没有算法能判定该形式系统里的每一个问题。
senses.why: logic borrowed the word for any mechanical decision method, because such a method removes the need for insight at each step.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借这个词指任何机械判定方法，因为这类方法免去了每一步都要靠洞察。

senses.title: The rule set inside a service
senses.titleCN: 服务内部运行的规则集
senses.definition: the scoring or ranking rules that decide what a platform shows to a user
senses.definitionCN: 决定平台向用户展示什么的评分或排序规则
senses.example: The feed algorithm ranks posts by how long people linger.
senses.exampleCN: 信息流算法按人们停留的时间给帖子排序。
senses.why: platforms turned a formal procedure into a product feature, and users met the word as the invisible rule behind what they see.
senses.whyCN: 平台把形式化步骤变成产品功能，用户于是把这个词理解为眼前内容背后那条看不见的规则。

senses.title: A procedure for routing or scheduling
senses.definition: the rule set a network or system uses to choose paths, times or resources
senses.definitionCN: 网络或系统用来选择路径、时间或资源的规则集
senses.example: The routing algorithm sends each packet along the least crowded link.
senses.exampleCN: 路由算法让每个数据包走最不拥挤的链路。
senses.why: networks must choose among options thousands of times a second, and any such choice rule is naturally called an algorithm.
senses.whyCN: 网络每秒要在众多选项中做出成千上万次选择，这类选择规则自然就叫算法。

senses.title: A recipe for doing something
senses.definition: a fixed, often unthinking way of proceeding in everyday matters
senses.definitionCN: 日常事务中固定、常常无需思考的处理方式
senses.example: There is no algorithm for choosing whom to trust.
senses.exampleCN: 挑选该信任谁，并没有现成的算法。
senses.why: when people say there is no algorithm for something, they mean no reliable step-by-step rule exists, which is the word used in its broadest everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说某事没有算法时，意思是并不存在可靠的逐步规则，这是这个词最宽泛的日常用法。

intro.en: Algorithm is an eponym: it comes from the Latinised name of the ninth-century mathematician al-Khwarizmi, whose textbook taught decimal calculation. The -th- spelling is a later mistake, not part of the name. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algorithm 是一个由人名转来的词：出自九世纪数学家花拉子米的拉丁化名字，他的教科书传授十进制计算。词中的 -th- 是后来的误写，并非名字的一部分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi worked in Baghdad in the ninth century and wrote a treatise on calculation with Indian numerals.
items.cn: 穆罕默德·伊本·穆萨·花拉子米在九世纪的巴格达工作，写有一部讲述用印度数字计算的论著。

items.en: Translators Latinised his name as Algoritmi, which became the label for his calculation method rather than for the man.
items.cn: 译者把他的名字拉丁化为 Algoritmi，这个词后来成了他所教计算法的标签，而不再指这个人。

items.en: Medieval Latin algorismus named the decimal system and the rules for using it, and English algorism came from that form.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 指十进制及其使用规则，英语 algorism 即由这一形式而来。

items.en: Writers linked the unfamiliar word to Greek arithmos, number, and altered the spelling to algorithm; the false link is documented and was never corrected.
items.cn: 写作者把这个陌生词与希腊语 arithmos「数」联系起来，把拼写改成 algorithm；这一错误联系有记录，且从未被纠正。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word shifted from written arithmetic rules to any precise procedure that a machine can execute.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词从书面的算术规则转为指任何机器可以执行的精确步骤。

items.en: Generally accepted: the personal name refers to Khwarazm, a region south of the Aral Sea, which older sources spell in more than one way. The derivation of the word from his name is documented; only the ancient spellings of the place vary.
items.cn: 一般认为是：这个人名指咸海南面的花拉子模地区，古代文献对该地名有不止一种拼写。这个词由他的名字转来有文献依据，可变的只是地名的古代拼写。

note.en: The first group shares the name or the spelling and is easily confused; the second group names neighbouring ideas of method, rule and shortcut.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一人名来源或形近，容易混淆；第二组是与方法、规则、捷径相邻的概念。

entries.definition: The older English word for the decimal system and its calculation rules; algorithm is the later, respelled descendant.
entries.definitionCN: 指十进制及其计算规则的较早英语词；algorithm 是后来改拼的变体。

entries.definition: Relating to algorithms; it describes the method, while algorithm names the method itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「算法的」；它描述方法，而 algorithm 指方法本身。

entries.definition: By means of an algorithm; it modifies how something is done, not what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按算法地」；它修饰做事方式，不指事物本身。

entries.definition: A mathematical exponent word built from Greek logos and arithmos; the shared ending is coincidence of spelling, not shared origin.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语 logos 与 arithmos 构成的数学指数词；相同词尾只是拼写巧合，并非同源。

entries.definition: Any agreed way of doing something; an algorithm is a procedure precise enough to be executed mechanically.
entries.definitionCN: 任何约定俗成的做法；algorithm 是精确到可机械执行的 procedure。

entries.definition: A way of working, often with judgment left to the user; an algorithm removes that judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 工作方式，常给使用者留出判断空间；algorithm 则取消这种判断。

entries.definition: A shortcut that usually works but has no guarantee; an algorithm promises a result for every allowed input.
entries.definitionCN: 通常有效但无保证的捷径；algorithm 则承诺对每个允许输入都给出结果。

entries.definition: The concrete code a machine runs; an algorithm is the method that the code implements, and one algorithm can be coded many ways.
entries.definitionCN: 机器运行的具体代码；algorithm 是代码所实现的方法，同一种算法可以有多种写法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real personal name, the real older spelling and the real computing phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的人名来源、真实的较早拼写与真实的计算机搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is a person: al-Khwarizmi taught the rules of calculation, and his Latinised name became the name of the rules.
normal.cn: 这个词来自一个人：花拉子米教计算规则，他的拉丁化名字就成了规则的名字。

normal.en: The older spelling algorism still means decimal calculation; algorithm is the respelled branch.
normal.cn: 较早拼写 algorism 仍指十进制计算；algorithm 是改拼后的分支。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the computing sense: sorting algorithm, search algorithm, encryption algorithm.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出计算机义：排序算法、搜索算法、加密算法。

normal.en: The -th- came from a mistaken link to Greek arithmos, number, and it stuck.
normal.cn: 词中的 -th- 来自与希腊语 arithmos「数」的错误联系，而且一直沿用下来。

normal.en: A logarithm looks like an algorithm but belongs to a different Greek family.
normal.cn: logarithm 看起来像 algorithm，却属于另一个希腊词族。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of doors, each opening only after the one before has closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每扇门都要前一扇关上后才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe that refuses to end until the pot is exactly full.
abstract.cn: 想象一份菜谱，锅没正好装满就绝不肯结束。

abstract.en: Picture a sorting hat that never asks for a second opinion.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶分院帽，从不征询第二个意见。

examples.en: The same algorithm can be written in five languages and still do the same work.
examples.cn: 同一个算法可以用五种语言写出，做的事仍然一样。

examples.en: A good algorithm says what to do when the input is empty.
examples.cn: 好的算法会说明输入为空时该怎么办。

examples.en: The team measured the algorithm's cost before adding more data.
examples.cn: 团队在增加数据之前先测了这套算法的开销。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱（al）哥（go）算（rith）法（m）」——爱算的哥们，一步步算到底

root: 九世纪数学家 al-Khwārizmī 之名 → 拉丁化 Algoritmi → 中世纪拉丁 algorismus → 英语 algorism；拼写受希腊语 arithmos「数」误类推而改为 algorithm。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one idea: a written method of calculation becomes any finite procedure, then a precise machine procedure, a formal object, a named routine, a decision rule, a product rule, a network rule and finally a recipe for life.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一个念头展开：一种写下来的计算方法，变成任何有限步骤，再变成精确的机器步骤、形式对象、具名例程、判定规则、产品规则、网络规则，最后变成生活里的套路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of boxes joined by arrows, each step pointing to the next and ending in a single result.
core.cn: 核心意象：方框由箭头串起，每一步指向下一步，最后收在一个结果上。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: written rules for decimal arithmetic, preserved in the spelling algorism.
branches.cn: 最老的一层：书面的十进制运算规则，保存在拼写 algorism 里。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: steps that always end, and steps explicit enough for a machine to follow without guessing.
branches.cn: 步骤：总会终止的步骤，以及明确到机器无需猜测就能执行的步骤。

branches.en: OBJECT AND ROUTINE: the same procedure studied as a mathematical object and shipped as a named library routine.
branches.cn: 对象与例程：同一套步骤既作为数学对象被研究，又作为具名库例程被交付。

branches.en: DECIDING AND ROUTING: logic and networks both use mechanical rules to choose among possibilities.
branches.cn: 判定与路由：逻辑学与网络都用机械规则在多种可能中作选择。

branches.en: EVERYDAY RULE: a platform's ranking rule and a personal recipe are both the word at its broadest.
branches.cn: 日常规则：平台的排序规则与个人的做事套路，都是这个词最宽泛的用法。

intro.en: Algorithm is not built from Latin or Greek roots but from a Latinised Arabic personal name; later spellings and endings were added by English and by a mistaken Greek link.
intro.cn: algorithm 并非由拉丁或希腊词根构成，而是来自拉丁化的阿拉伯人名；后来的拼写与词尾是英语加上去的，另有一处希腊语误联。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin algorismus is the bridge form; the Greek arithmos that reshaped the spelling is a false association, not a real element.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 是中间的桥接形式；改写拼写的希腊语 arithmos 是错误联想，并非真实构件。

items.example: The article is frozen into the Latinised name.
items.exampleCN: 这个冠词被冻进了拉丁化的人名里。

items.example: The nisba identifies the scholar by his region.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字后缀用地名标识这位学者。

items.structure: Latinised form of the Arabic name
items.meaningCN: 这位学者名字的拉丁写法
items.example: Translators used the name for the method.
items.exampleCN: 译者用这个名字来指那套方法。

items.meaning: the decimal system and its rules
items.example: The Latin noun became English algorism.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词成了英语 algorism。

items.example: The Greek word pulled the spelling toward -th- by mistake.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词把拼写误拉向 -th-。

items.example: Algorism is the older doublet of algorithm.
items.exampleCN: algorism 是 algorithm 的较早同源异形词。

items.example: The respelling attached the word to number.
items.exampleCN: 这次改拼把词与「数」挂上了钩。

items.example: Algorithmic describes anything driven by such a procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmic 描述由这类步骤驱动的事物。

items.example: Algorithmically means by running the procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmically 意为「按算法执行」。

items.example: Algorithmics names the theory of procedures.
items.exampleCN: algorithmics 指关于步骤的理论。

definition_zh: 选择压力；环境对群体中不同变异体生存与繁殖的差别性作用强度
definition_en: the strength of the environmental force that makes some variants survive and reproduce better than others
core_image: 一只手从上方压下，桌上一排高低不同的小柱，高柱被压弯、矮柱纹丝不动，旁边记着刻度与计数
scene: 实验室里，同一批细菌被分成两组，一组加抗生素、一组不加，加药的那组只有少数菌落存活。 The antibiotic put strong selection pressure on the culture, and only resistant cells remained.
sceneCN: 这里 selection pressure 指「选择压力」（第 1 个义项：使不同变异体在生存上产生差别的作用强度）；句意：抗生素对这一培养物施加了很强的选择压力，最后只剩下耐药细胞。图中可辨识物件：培养皿、抗生素纸片、存活菌落、计数表格。

pos.zh: 选择压力（可数或不可数，复数为 selection pressures）

collocations.zh: 来自捕食者的选择压力

senses.title: The force behind differential survival
senses.definition: the force that causes variants in a population to survive and reproduce at different rates
senses.definitionCN: 使群体内各变异体以不同速率存活与繁殖的作用力
senses.example: Predation placed heavy selection pressure on the slower moths.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食对行动较慢的蛾施加了沉重的选择压力。
senses.why: pressure names a push that is applied, so the phrase pictures the environment pressing on a population and sorting it.
senses.whyCN: pressure 指施加的推力，因此这个短语把环境想象成压在群体上并把它分选开来。

senses.title: Its measurable intensity
senses.definition: the quantified strength of selection, often expressed as a selection coefficient
senses.definitionCN: 选择的量化强度，常以选择系数表示
senses.example: The study estimated the selection pressure on beak depth.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究估算了喙深所受的选择压力强度。
senses.why: once the force is measured, it becomes a variable that can be compared across traits and populations.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种力被测量，它就变成一个可跨性状、跨群体比较的变量。

senses.title: The source of the pressure
senses.definition: the specific agent, such as a predator, a disease or a climate, that applies the pressure
senses.definitionCN: 施加压力的具体因素，如捕食者、疾病或气候
senses.example: Drought is the main selection pressure in this grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱是这片草地上的主要选择压力。
senses.why: the phrase can name either the force or its source, and ecology usually cares about which agent is doing the pushing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既可指力，也可指力的来源，而生态学通常关心是哪个因素在推。

senses.title: A directional bias on one trait
senses.titleCN: 方向性偏压：把某一性状往一边推
senses.definition: pressure that consistently favours one end of a trait's range over the other
senses.definitionCN: 持续偏向某一性状取值区间一端、而非另一端的压力
senses.example: Longer bills faced positive selection pressure during the dry years.
senses.exampleCN: 在干旱年份，较长的喙承受正向选择压力。
senses.why: when the same end keeps winning, the pressure acquires a direction, which is how new traits begin to shift.
senses.whyCN: 当同一端持续胜出，压力就有了方向，新性状正是这样开始移动的。

senses.title: A constraint that removes variants
senses.titleCN: 淘汰作用：把不适合的变异去掉
senses.definition: the part of the pressure that eliminates variants rather than promoting them
senses.definitionCN: 压力中负责淘汰而非促进变异的那一部分
senses.example: Frost imposes a selection pressure that weeds out early flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻施加选择压力，把早开花的个体淘汰掉。
senses.why: selection is often easier to see as removal: what disappears leaves a visible gap in the distribution.
senses.whyCN: 选择往往更容易被看成「移除」：消失的部分在分布上留下可见的空缺。

senses.title: Human-induced pressure
senses.titleCN: 人为压力：抗生素、捕捞与污染
senses.definition: selection pressure created by human activity, such as drugs, harvesting or pollution
senses.definitionCN: 由人类活动造成的选择压力，如药物、采捕或污染
senses.example: Trawling applies selection pressure for smaller adult fish.
senses.exampleCN: 拖网对体型更小的成鱼施加选择压力。
senses.why: people became the strongest source of pressure in many systems, so the phrase now carries a conservation warning.
senses.whyCN: 在许多系统里人已成为最强的压力来源，因此这个短语如今带有保护警示。

senses.title: Analogy outside biology
senses.titleCN: 生物学之外的类比用法
senses.definition: the extended use of the phrase for any environment that favours some variants over others
senses.definitionCN: 把这个短语扩展用于任何偏爱某些变体的环境
senses.example: The market put selection pressure on firms with thin cash reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 市场对现金储备薄弱的公司施加选择压力。
senses.why: once 'variant plus environment' is abstracted, the phrase fits markets, software and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 当「变体加环境」被抽象出来，这个短语就适用于市场、软件与机构。

senses.title: Relaxed or released pressure
senses.titleCN: 压力松弛：筛选变弱之后
senses.definition: the state in which selection pressure is reduced, allowing traits to drift or decline
senses.definitionCN: 选择压力减弱、使性状得以漂变或退化的状态
senses.example: With predators gone, selection pressure on armour relaxed.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食者消失后，对甲壳的选择压力松弛了。
senses.why: pressure is only visible when it is removed: traits that cost something then persist without being pruned.
senses.whyCN: 压力只在被移除时才显形：此后那些有代价的性状不再被修剪，得以留存。

intro.en: Selection pressure joins selectio 'a choosing out' to pressure, from Latin pressura 'a pressing', built on premere 'to press'. The ecological phrase is twentieth-century, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: selection pressure 把 selectio「挑出」与出自拉丁 pressura「压挤」、基于 premere「压」的 pressure 组合起来；这一生态短语形成于 20 世纪，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Legere 'to gather, pick out' underlies select, selection and selective through the compound seligere.
items.cn: legere「收集、挑出」经复合词 seligere 构成 select、selection 与 selective 的基础。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze'; pressura named the act or result of pressing.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」；pressura 指压的动作或结果。

items.en: Pressure entered English in the fourteenth century as a physical term and later acquired figurative senses.
items.cn: pressure 于 14 世纪作为物理术语进入英语，后来获得比喻义。

items.en: Nineteenth-century naturalists spoke of selection acting on variations, but the fixed phrase selection pressure is later.
items.cn: 19 世纪博物学者谈论选择作用于变异，但固定短语 selection pressure 出现得更晚。

items.en: Population genetics in the twentieth century made the phrase quantitative, tied to fitness differences and selection coefficients.
items.cn: 20 世纪的群体遗传学使这个短语定量化，与适合度差异和选择系数挂钩。

items.en: The exact first use of the compound is uncertain; earlier writers said 'pressure of selection' or 'selective pressure'.
items.cn: 这一复合词的确切首用不确定；更早的作者写作「选择的压力」或「选择性压力」。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same roots; group two holds related terms that name a different part of the evolutionary account.
note.cn: 第一组是同源形近词；第二组是相关术语，各自命名进化解释中的不同部分。

entries.definition: The same idea with an adjective instead of a noun, widely used in textbooks; the two are usually interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念改用形容词表达，教科书常用；二者通常可互换。

entries.definition: The outcome of differential survival. Pressure is the force that produces that outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 指差别生存的结果；压力是产生这一结果的作用力。

entries.definition: A force applied to something. On its own it need not be biological at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指施加于某物的力；单独使用时完全不必与生物有关。

entries.definition: Deliberate choice of parents by breeders. It produces artificial, not natural, selection pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指育种者有意挑选亲本，产生的是人工而非自然的选择压力。

entries.definition: The mechanism as a whole. Selection pressure is one way of measuring how hard that mechanism is pushing.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个机制；选择压力是衡量这一机制推力大小的一种方式。

entries.definition: The relative reproductive success of a variant. Pressure explains why fitness differs.
entries.definitionCN: 指变体的相对繁殖成功率；压力解释为何适合度会有差异。

entries.definition: A factor that limits what evolution can build, such as body plan or available variation; it is not the same as a pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制进化能造出什么的因素，如体型方案或可用变异；与压力不同。

entries.definition: An environmental condition that strains organisms. It may create selection pressure, but it is not the pressure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指使生物承受压力的环境条件；它可能造成选择压力，但本身不是压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: selection 'picking out' + pressure 'pressing': the environment pressing on a population and picking.
normal.cn: selection「挑选」+ pressure「压」：环境压向群体并挑选。

normal.en: The family runs select, selection, selective, pressure, press.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 select、selection、selective、pressure、press。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: strong pressure, pressure on a trait, under pressure, relieve pressure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：强压力、对某性状的压力、处于压力之下、缓解压力。

normal.en: Pair it with fitness: pressure explains why fitness scores differ.
normal.cn: 把它与 fitness 配对：压力解释为何适合度分数不同。

normal.en: Pair it with constraint: pressure pushes, constraint limits.
normal.cn: 把它与 constraint 配对：压力推动，约束限制。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flattening tall posts but leaving short ones upright.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把高柱压弯，矮柱却直立不动。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve that lets small seeds through and holds large ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子让小的种子漏下，把大的留下。

abstract.en: Picture a trawl net that keeps only fish below a certain size.
abstract.cn: 想象一张拖网只留下小于某个尺寸的鱼。

examples.en: Selection pressure from predators favours faster runners.
examples.cn: 来自捕食者的选择压力偏爱跑得更快的个体。

examples.en: Removing the drug relieves selection pressure on resistant bacteria.
examples.cn: 停用药物会缓解耐药细菌所受的选择压力。

examples.en: The team measured selection pressure as a difference in survival rates.
examples.cn: 团队以存活率的差异来衡量选择压力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挑选 + 压力」——环境像一只手掌，把不合格的压下去 → 选择压力

root: 拉丁 seligere「挑出」（se- + legere）+ 拉丁 premere「压」→ pressura「压挤」；生态与群体遗传学术语于 20 世纪定量化。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a force is applied, measured, sourced, directed, seen as removal, traced to people, extended as an analogy and finally released.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次推压展开：力被施加、被测量、被溯源、被定向、被看成淘汰、被人为放大、被当作类比，最后被松开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing down on a row of uneven posts, bending only some.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手压向一排高低不齐的柱子，只把其中一些压弯。

branches.en: FORCE AND MEASURE: the push exists, and then it is given a number.
branches.cn: 力与量：推力存在，随后被赋予数值。

branches.en: SOURCE AND DIRECTION: which agent pushes, and toward which end of the range.
branches.cn: 来源与方向：哪个因素在推，又推向取值区间的哪一端。

branches.en: REMOVAL AND RELEASE: pressure is clearest in what it deletes, and in what returns once it stops.
branches.cn: 淘汰与松弛：压力在它删去什么、以及停下后什么回流时最清楚。

branches.en: HUMAN SOURCE: drugs, nets and pollution become the strongest pressures.
branches.cn: 人为来源：药物、渔网与污染成为最强的压力。

branches.en: ANALOGY: markets and software inherit the same shape.
branches.cn: 类比：市场与软件继承了同一形状。

intro.en: The compound is two Latin-derived nouns; selection carries -ion and pressure carries -ure, both noun endings of action or result.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个拉丁来源名词构成：selection 带 -ion，pressure 带 -ure，两者都是表动作或结果的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin seligere gives select, selection and selective; Latin premere gives press, pressure, compress, express and suppress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 seligere 衍生 select、selection 与 selective；拉丁 premere 衍生 press、pressure、compress、express 与 suppress。

items.example: Selection pressure shaped the beak within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 选择压力在十年内塑造了鸟喙。

items.example: Selection removed the weakest seedlings.
items.exampleCN: 筛选淘汰了最弱的幼苗。

items.example: The females select the loudest singers.
items.exampleCN: 雌性挑选叫声最响的个体。

items.example: Grazing is selective on tall grasses.
items.exampleCN: 放牧对高草具有选择性。

items.example: The pressure on the population never eased.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体所受的压力从未减轻。

items.example: The crowding pressed the plants into narrow forms.
items.exampleCN: 拥挤把植株压成窄小的形态。

items.example: The sediment compressed into shale.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物被压成页岩。

items.meaning: to press down; to hold back
items.example: Fire suppression removed a natural pressure.
items.exampleCN: 灭火措施移除了一种自然压力。

definition_zh: 卓越；优秀；长处；杰出表现
definition_en: the quality of being extremely good, or a particular way of being very good
core_image: 一座高出周围屋顶的塔尖，从一片屋檐之上露出来
scene: 毕业典礼上，校长把奖章挂到那个连续三年拿下数学竞赛冠军的学生胸前。 Her excellence in mathematics won her a scholarship to a top university.
sceneCN: 这里 excellence 是「卓越、杰出」（第 1 个义项：极高的水准）；句意：她在数学上的卓越表现为她赢得了顶尖大学的奖学金。

pos.zh: 卓越；优秀；长处；杰出表现

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词词尾 -ence 得到的动词，义为「出类拔萃；擅长」
拉丁语现在分词转成的形容词，义为「极好的；优秀的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「极好地」

senses.title: The quality of being extremely good
senses.definition: a very high standard of quality or ability that stands out from the ordinary
senses.definitionCN: 远超一般水平的质量或能力
senses.example: The school is known for the excellence of its teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以卓越的教学质量著称。
senses.why: Latin excellere means to rise above, so excellence is literally the state of standing higher than the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 excellere 意为「高出、超越」，所以 excellence 字面上就是「站得比其余的都高」的状态。

senses.title: A particular strength
senses.definition: one specific quality in which a person or thing is very good
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物在某一方面特别出色的具体优点
senses.example: His chief excellence as a teacher is patience.
senses.exampleCN: 作为教师，他最大的长处是耐心。
senses.why: Once the quality can be counted, the abstract noun names one item on a list of strengths, which is how the plural excellences works.
senses.whyCN: 当这种品质可以被数出来时，抽象名词就指长处清单上的一项，复数 excellences 正是这样用的。

senses.title: Outstanding performance in a field
senses.definition: a level of achievement that stands out in a subject, a sport, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在学科、运动或职业中脱颖而出的成就水平
senses.example: The prize rewards excellence in scientific research.
senses.exampleCN: 该奖项奖励在科学研究中的杰出表现。
senses.why: The preposition in ties the noun to a field, so excellence becomes a measurable standing inside that field rather than general praise.
senses.whyCN: 介词 in 把这个名词绑定到某个领域，于是 excellence 变成该领域内可衡量的水平，而不只是笼统的称赞。

senses.title: A recognized model of high quality
senses.definition: a place, group, or practice officially recognized as an outstanding example
senses.definitionCN: 被正式认定为杰出范例的地方、团体或做法
senses.example: The hospital was named a centre of excellence for heart surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院被评为心脏外科的卓越中心。
senses.why: Modern institutions turned the abstract quality into a title, so a building or a whole team can now carry the word as a name.
senses.whyCN: 现代机构把这种抽象品质变成了一个称号，于是一栋建筑或一整个团队如今可以把这个词当作名号来用。

intro.en: Excellence goes back to Latin excellere, to rise above, and reached English through Old French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: excellence 可追溯到拉丁语 excellere（高出、超越），中世纪经古法语进入英语。

items.en: The stem cellere means to rise or be high, seen also in celsus, lofty, and collis, hill.
items.cn: 词干 cellere 意为高起、处于高处，也见于 celsus（高耸的）与 collis（山丘）。

items.en: Excellere combines ex-, out, with cellere, and means to rise above or surpass.
items.cn: excellere 由 ex-（向外）与 cellere 组合，意为高出、超越。

items.en: Excellentia names superiority or pre-eminence in the classical period.
items.cn: 古典时期用 excellentia 表示优越、出众。

items.en: Old French takes the noun as excellence with the same meaning.
items.cn: 古法语以 excellence 的形式吸收这个名词，含义不变。

items.en: English records excellence in the fourteenth century as a word for superior quality.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记下 excellence，指优越的品质。

items.en: Modern English adds fixed phrases such as centre of excellence and academic excellence.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上 centre of excellence 与 academic excellence 这类固定说法。

note.en: Excellence belongs to the same root as excel and excellent, and sits beside the nouns of merit and superiority.
note.cn: excellence 与 excel、excellent 同根，并与表示「优点、优越」的名词为邻。

entries.definition: to be very good at something
entries.definitionCN: 擅长；出类拔萃

entries.definition: extremely good
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；优秀的

entries.definition: a title of honour for high officials
entries.definitionCN: 对高级官员的尊称「阁下」

entries.definition: a good quality that deserves praise
entries.definitionCN: 值得称赞的优点

entries.definition: the state of being better than others
entries.definitionCN: 优越；优势

entries.definition: excellence shown in work or results
entries.definitionCN: 优异；卓越表现

normalIntro.en: Excellence and excel share one Latin verb for rising above, so the noun is a height rather than a score.
normalIntro.cn: excellence 与 excel 共享同一个表示「高出」的拉丁动词，所以这个名词是高度，而不是分数。

normal.en: The verb behind the noun is excel, to rise above others.
normal.cn: 名词背后的动词是 excel，意为高出他人。

normal.en: The adjective excellent keeps the same idea of standing out.
normal.cn: 形容词 excellent 保留了同样的突出意味。

normal.en: Excellence in a subject names the field after the preposition in.
normal.cn: excellence in 后面的介词 in 点出的是哪个领域。

normal.en: A centre of excellence is an institution that carries the word as a title.
normal.cn: a centre of excellence 是把这个词当作名号的机构。

normal.en: Compare superiority: superiority compares two things, excellence praises the standard itself.
normal.cn: 对比 superiority：superiority 比较两样东西，excellence 则直接称赞水准本身。

abstract.en: Picture one tower top rising above a row of roofs.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔尖从一排屋顶之上冒出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a list of strengths with one entry written on each line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长处清单，每一行写着一个条目。

abstract.en: Think of a scoreboard where one name sits far above the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌，有一个名字远远排在别人上面。

examples.en: The judges praised the excellence of the design.
examples.cn: 评委称赞这项设计的卓越。

examples.en: She won a national award for excellence in teaching.
examples.cn: 她获得了表彰卓越教学的国家奖。

examples.en: No one doubts his excellence as a pianist.
examples.cn: 没有人怀疑他作为钢琴家的卓越水平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗赛伦斯」——赛场上最亮的那「一颗」星，水平超出同辈之上；拆开看是 ex 加 cellere（高起），这才是词源线索，谐音只是辅助联想。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、超出）+ cellere（高起、隆起）→ excellere（高出、超越）→ excellentia（优越）→ 古法语 excellence → 英语 excellence，核心义「高出众人之上」。

sensesIntro.en: Excellence begins as a high standard, then a countable strength, then outstanding work in one field, and finally an institution honoured with the word.
sensesIntro.cn: excellence 先指很高的水准，再指可数的一项长处，然后指某个领域里的杰出表现，最后指被授予这个词的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower top standing above the surrounding roofs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座塔尖高过四周的屋顶。

branches.en: Standing higher than the rest is the core sense of high quality.
branches.cn: 站得比别人高，就是「高品质」这一核心义。

branches.en: The same height can be counted one peak at a time, giving a strength.
branches.cn: 同样的高度可以一座峰一座峰地数，于是有了一项长处。

branches.en: Set inside a field, the height becomes a measurable achievement.
branches.cn: 把它放进某个领域，这个高度就变成可衡量的成就。

branches.en: Institutions borrowed the word as a title, so the quality became a name.
branches.cn: 机构把这个词借来当称号，于是品质变成了名号。

branches.en: Both the general standard and the field-specific award rest on the same upward image.
branches.cn: 笼统的水准与特定领域的奖项，都建立在同一个「向上」的意象上。

intro.en: Excellence grows from the Latin verb excellere, with English excel, excellent, and excellently built on the same stem.
intro.cn: excellence 从拉丁语动词 excellere 长出，英语的 excel、excellent 与 excellently 都建在同一词干上。

latinIntro.en: Latin excellere means to rise above, formed from ex-, out, and cellere, to rise or be high.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excellere 意为高出、超越，由 ex-（向外）与 cellere（高起）构成。

items.example: The prefix ex- marks the movement upward and beyond.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 标出向上、超出的方向。

items.example: Cellere supplies the image of height.
items.exampleCN: cellere 提供「高度」这一意象。

items.example: Celsus shows the same high root as a adjective.
items.exampleCN: celsus 以形容词形式显示同一个「高」的词根。

items.example: Excellere is the direct source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: excellere 是整个词族的直接来源。

items.example: Excellentia carries the noun sense into French.
items.exampleCN: excellentia 把名词义带入法语。

items.example: The suffix -ence turns the stem into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ence 把词干变成状态名词。

items.example: Excellence keeps the abstract sense of the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: excellence 保留拉丁名词的抽象含义。

items.example: Excel is the short English verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: excel 是这个词族里简短的英语动词。

items.example: Excellent describes the thing that stands above others.
items.exampleCN: excellent 描述高出其他事物的人或物。

definition_zh: 调查的；调查性的；侦查的；用于查明事实的
definition_en: relating to or used for investigation, especially the systematic search for facts about a crime, accident, complaint, or research question
core_image: 一束探照灯沿着脚印一路照过去，不放过任何一处痕迹
scene: 新闻编辑部里，主编说这个团队追一条资金链追了半年。 Their investigative reporting followed the money for six months.
sceneCN: 这里 investigative 是「调查性的」（第 1 个义项：用于查明事实的）；句意：他们的调查性报道追了这条资金链半年。

pos.zh: 调查的；调查性的（用于报道、工作、方法等）
侦查的；有调查职能或权限的（用于机构、委员会、权力）

senses.title: Relating to investigative journalism
senses.definition: describing reporting that follows documents and sources over a long period to expose hidden facts
senses.definitionCN: 描述长期追踪文件与消息源、以揭露隐藏事实的报道
senses.example: The paper's investigative team spent a year on the story.
senses.exampleCN: 该报的调查团队为这篇报道花了一年。
senses.why: Investigative is investigate + -ive. The Latin source investigare means 'track in', from vestigium 'footprint'. The adjective marks work whose purpose is to follow a trail rather than to report what is already public.
senses.whyCN: investigative 是 investigate + -ive。拉丁语源 investigare 意为“循迹进入”，来自 vestigium“脚印”。这个形容词标记目的是循迹追查、而非报道已知公开信息的工作。

senses.title: Relating to police investigation
senses.definition: describing the work, unit, or method used by authorities to solve a crime
senses.definitionCN: 描述当局为破案而做的工作、部门或方法
senses.example: The investigative unit reviewed the cold case.
senses.exampleCN: 侦查部门重新审查了这桩旧案。
senses.why: Police usage makes the trail concrete: scenes, witnesses, and records. The adjective attaches to 'unit', 'work', and 'powers', marking the official function rather than a person's curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 警务用法让痕迹具体化：现场、证人、记录。这个形容词常修饰 unit、work、powers，标记官方职能，而不是个人的好奇。

senses.title: Describing methods or techniques
senses.definition: describing tools or procedures designed to obtain evidence, such as interviews, searches, or forensic tests
senses.definitionCN: 描述为取得证据而设计的工具或程序，如访谈、搜查或法医检验
senses.example: They used standard investigative techniques to trace the payment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用标准的侦查手段追踪这笔付款。
senses.why: Here the adjective modifies the means rather than the ends. A technique is investigative when its purpose is to produce evidence that can be checked by others.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词修饰手段而不是目的。当一项技术的目的在于产出可被他人核对的证据时，它就是 investigative 的。

senses.title: Describing a body or committee
senses.definition: describing an official group set up to examine a matter and report findings
senses.definitionCN: 描述为审查某一事项并报告结论而设立的官方小组
senses.example: An investigative committee was formed after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故后成立了一个调查委员会。
senses.why: Institutions create such bodies when ordinary management cannot be trusted to examine itself. The adjective names a temporary authority with a defined scope.
senses.whyCN: 当普通管理层不足以被信任来审查自身时，机构会设立这类小组。这个形容词命名一个有明确范围的临时权力。

senses.title: Describing legal powers
senses.definition: describing the authority to compel documents, testimony, or access during an inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 描述调查过程中强制取得文件、证言或进入场所的权力
senses.example: The regulator has broad investigative powers but limited sanctions.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构拥有广泛的调查权，但制裁手段有限。
senses.why: Law separates the power to find facts from the power to punish. The adjective marks the first, which is why 'investigative powers' often appear next to 'limited enforcement'.
senses.whyCN: 法律把查明事实的权力与惩罚的权力分开。这个形容词标记前者，所以 investigative powers 常与 limited enforcement 并提。

senses.title: Describing a research approach
senses.definition: describing a scholarly approach that actively seeks answers rather than only describing
senses.definitionCN: 描述主动寻求答案、而非仅仅描述的学术路径
senses.example: The course takes an investigative approach to local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课以探究方式处理地方史。
senses.why: Educators use the adjective for learning by inquiry: students pose questions and gather evidence. The word turns the classroom into a place where trails are followed.
senses.whyCN: 教育者用这个形容词指探究式学习：学生提出问题并收集证据。这个词把课堂变成循迹追查的场所。

senses.title: Describing medical procedures
senses.definition: describing tests or procedures whose purpose is diagnosis rather than treatment
senses.definitionCN: 描述目的为诊断而非治疗的操作或检查
senses.example: The procedure is investigative, not therapeutic.
senses.exampleCN: 这项操作是检查性的，不是治疗性的。
senses.why: Medicine distinguishes what is done to find out from what is done to cure. The adjective keeps the trail image inside the body: each test follows a sign toward its source.
senses.whyCN: 医学区分“为查明而做”与“为治愈而做”。这个形容词把痕迹意象带进体内：每项检查顺着征象追到源头。

senses.title: Describing an investigative mindset
senses.definition: describing a habit of questioning claims and looking for evidence behind them
senses.definitionCN: 描述质疑说法、寻找其背后证据的习惯
senses.example: Her investigative habit made her distrust press releases.
senses.exampleCN: 她的追查习惯让她不轻信新闻稿。
senses.why: This sense is about disposition rather than occupation: anyone can read a claim as a trail. The adjective praises scepticism, but also warns that constant suspicion has a cost.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎性情而非职业：任何人都可以把一个说法读成一条痕迹。这个形容词称赞怀疑精神，但也提醒持续怀疑是有代价的。

intro.en: Investigative is investigate + -ive, formed in English on the Latin verb investigare. The root is vestigium 'footprint', so the adjective describes anything used to follow a trail toward its source.
intro.cn: investigative 是 investigate + -ive，在英语中由拉丁动词 investigare 构成。词根是 vestigium“脚印”，因此这个形容词描述任何用于循迹追源的东西。

items.en: Latin vestigium 'footprint' produced vestigare 'to track' and investigare 'to track into, search out'. The participle investigatus gave English the verb stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium“脚印”产生 vestigare“追踪”与 investigare“追查进去”。分词 investigatus 给英语提供了动词词干。

items.en: English investigate entered in the fifteenth century; the adjective investigative followed much later, when the -ive pattern was extended to legal and practical contexts.
items.cn: 英语 investigate 于 15 世纪进入；形容词 investigative 晚得多才出现，当时 -ive 模式被扩展到法律与实践语境。

items.en: Investigative is generally associated with the rise of professional reporting in the nineteenth century, when newspapers began following documents as police followed footprints.
items.cn: investigative 一般与 19 世纪职业报道的兴起相关联，当时报纸开始像警察循脚印那样追查文件。

items.en: Police reform and muckraking journalism fixed phrases such as 'investigative unit' and 'investigative reporting'. The adjective became a mark of seriousness and public duty.
items.cn: 警务改革与黑幕揭发报道固定了 investigative unit、investigative reporting 等说法。这个形容词成为严肃性与公共责任的标志。

items.en: Research methods and clinical writing adopted 'investigative' to separate finding out from treating. The word now marks purpose, not profession.
items.cn: 研究方法与临床写作采用 investigative 来区分“查明”与“治疗”。这个词如今标记目的，而不是职业。

items.en: Modern usage spans newsrooms, police units, committees, classrooms, and clinics. In every case the adjective says the aim is to discover facts that are not yet established.
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖编辑部、警队、委员会、课堂与诊所。无论哪种情况，这个形容词都表示目的在于发现尚未确定的事实。

note.en: The look-alike group separates same-root variants from words built on other roots; the near-meaning group separates investigative, exploratory, and inquisitive.
note.cn: 形近组区分同根变体与建立在其他词根上的词；近义组区分 investigative、exploratory 与 inquisitive。

entries.definition: having the nature of an inquiry. It is close to investigative but more formal and more often used of powers and procedures than of reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 具有调查性质的。它接近 investigative，但更正式，且更常用于权力与程序，而非报道。

entries.definition: money or effort put into something for a return. It comes from investire 'to clothe', from vestis 'garment', not from vestigium 'footprint'.
entries.definitionCN: 为获得回报而投入的金钱或精力。它来自 investire“穿衣”，词根是 vestis“衣服”，而非 vestigium“脚印”。

entries.definition: eager to learn or ask questions. It comes from quaerere 'seek, ask', and describes curiosity rather than a formal search for evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 渴望了解或提问的。它来自 quaerere“寻求、询问”，描述好奇心，而不是正式的取证。

entries.definition: done to discover what is there, without a fixed hypothesis. It is more open-ended than investigative, which usually seeks facts about a specific matter.
entries.definitionCN: 为发现那里有什么而做，没有固定假设。它比 investigative 更开放，后者通常查找某件具体事情的事实。

entries.definition: relating to a person whose job is solving crimes. It names the role, while investigative describes the purpose or method.
entries.definitionCN: 与以破案为业的人有关的。它命名角色，而 investigative 描述目的或方法。

entries.definition: relating to a system where the court itself investigates. It is a technical legal term, much narrower than investigative.
entries.definitionCN: 与由法院自行调查的制度有关的。它是技术法律术语，比 investigative 窄得多。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: vestigium 'footprint', the -ive adjective ending, and the fixed phrases investigative journalism and investigative powers.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：vestigium“脚印”、-ive 形容词结尾，以及 investigative journalism、investigative powers 等固定说法。

normal.en: Same root as investigation: this adjective describes anything whose job is to follow the trail.
normal.cn: 与 investigation 同根：这个形容词描述任何以循迹为职责的东西。

normal.en: Investigative journalism follows documents the way police follow footprints.
normal.cn: 调查报道追文件，正如警察追脚印。

normal.en: Investigative powers mean you may compel evidence; they do not mean you may punish.
normal.cn: 调查权意味着可以强制取证，并不意味着可以惩罚。

normal.en: An investigative procedure in hospital is for diagnosis, not for cure.
normal.cn: 医院里的检查性操作是为了诊断，而不是为了治愈。

normal.en: An investigative habit reads every claim as a possible trail.
normal.cn: 追查习惯把每个说法都读成一条可能的痕迹。

abstract.en: The adjective marks purpose, not profession: a student, a nurse, or a reporter can all work investigatively.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词标记目的，而不是职业：学生、护士或记者都可以以调查方式工作。

abstract.en: It assumes facts are hidden but reachable, which is both its optimism and its limit.
abstract.cn: 它假定事实虽被隐藏却可抵达，这既是它的乐观，也是它的限度。

abstract.en: Every investigative act asks the same question: what trace would this claim leave if it were true?
abstract.cn: 每一次调查性行动都问同一个问题：如果这个说法为真，它会留下什么痕迹？

examples.en: Investigative reporting exposed the illegal dumping.
examples.cn: 调查性报道揭露了非法倾倒行为。

examples.en: The agency has investigative powers but no authority to prosecute.
examples.cn: 该机构有调查权，但没有起诉权。

examples.en: The scan is investigative only and will not treat the lesion.
examples.cn: 这次扫描仅为检查性质，不会治疗病灶。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因外斯提给提舞”——沿着外面的脚印“提”出证据，还带着追查的架势 → investigative 调查性的、侦查的

root: in-（进入）+ 拉丁语 vestigium“脚印”、vestigare“追踪”+ -ive；字面义“循迹进入的”，核心是“以查明事实为目的的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of investigative all describe a purpose: reporting, policing, techniques, committees, legal powers, research teaching, diagnosis, and sceptical habit. The adjective never names a person; it names what the work is for.
sensesIntro.cn: investigative 的八个义项都描述一种目的：报道、警务、手段、委员会、法律权力、研究教学、诊断与怀疑习惯。这个形容词从不命名人，它命名工作的目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a searchlight following footprints, leaving no trace unexamined.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束探照灯沿着脚印照过去，不放过任何痕迹。

branches.en: DISPOSITION AND PRESS: reporting and personal scepticism both treat claims as trails.
branches.cn: 态度与新闻：报道与个人怀疑都把说法当作痕迹。

branches.en: POLICE WORK: units and techniques exist to produce evidence that others can check.
branches.cn: 警务：部门与手段的存在，是为了产出可被他人核对的证据。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: committees and legal powers are the formal right to inquire, not to punish.
branches.cn: 权威：委员会与法律权力是正式调查权，而不是惩罚权。

branches.en: LEARNING: inquiry-based teaching turns students into followers of trails.
branches.cn: 学习：探究式教学把学生变成循迹者。

branches.en: MEDICINE: diagnostic procedures follow signs inside the body to their source.
branches.cn: 医学：诊断性操作顺着体内征象追到源头。

intro.en: Investigative is investigate + -ive, with investigatory as the -ory variant. Both come from Latin investigare and vestigium. The family also contains vestige and vestigial, which preserve the literal footprint.
intro.cn: investigative 是 investigate + -ive，investigatory 是 -ory 变体。两者都来自拉丁语 investigare 与 vestigium。家族还包含 vestige 与 vestigial，保留字面的“脚印”义。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium 'footprint' gave vestigare 'track' and investigare 'track into'. The look-alike invest is unrelated: it comes from investire 'clothe', based on vestis 'garment'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium“脚印”给出 vestigare“追踪”与 investigare“追进去”。形近的 invest 无关：它来自 investire“穿衣”，词根是 vestis“衣服”。

items.meaningCN: 调查的；调查性的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The unit does investigative work.
items.exampleCN: 这个部门做调查工作。

items.meaningCN: 调查；侦查（字面“循迹进入”）
items.example: They investigated the complaint.
items.exampleCN: 他们调查了这项投诉。

items.meaningCN: 调查；侦查（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The investigation is still open.
items.exampleCN: 调查仍在进行。

items.meaning: one who carries out an inquiry
items.meaningCN: 调查员；侦查员（-or 表施动者）
items.example: The investigator interviewed ten witnesses.
items.exampleCN: 调查员访谈了十名证人。

items.meaning: of the nature of an inquiry
items.meaningCN: 调查性质的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The panel has investigatory authority.
items.exampleCN: 该小组拥有调查权。

items.example: The archive was reinvestigated.
items.exampleCN: 这些档案被重新调查。

items.meaningCN: 痕迹；遗迹（直接借自拉丁名词）
items.example: A vestige of the old road survives.
items.exampleCN: 旧路的一点残迹仍在。

items.meaning: remaining as a trace, often without function
items.example: The tail is vestigial in this species.
items.exampleCN: 这个物种的尾巴已退化。

items.example: The fund invests in clean energy.
items.exampleCN: 该基金投资清洁能源。

definition_zh: 金丝雀；淡黄色；告密者（俚语）
definition_en: a small yellow songbird kept as a pet; also a light yellow color, or in slang, an informer
core_image: 笼中一只淡黄小鸟引颈高歌：歌声既是报晓的美妙声音，也是报警的信号
scene: 矿井口，矿工拎起鸟笼又看了看天色，才带队下井。 The canary stopped singing, and the miners scrambled back up.
sceneCN: 这里 canary 是「金丝雀」（第 1 个义项：作报警用的笼养小鸟）；句意是金丝雀停止鸣叫后，矿工们急忙爬回井上。

pos.zh: 金丝雀（雀科鸣禽）
淡黄色（颜色名）
告密者（俚语）

collocations.phrase: a canary in a coal mine
collocations.zh: 矿井里的金丝雀（预警信号）
像金丝雀一样招供（俚语）

derivatives.zh: 专有名词，义为「加那利群岛」，金丝雀原产地的地名来源
复合名词，义为「草芦」，一种原产该地区的草
复合名词，义为「金丝雀黄；淡黄色」

senses.title: A small yellow songbird
senses.definition: a small finch native to the Canary Islands, bred in cages for its bright color and song
senses.definitionCN: 原产加那利群岛的小型雀鸟，因羽色明黄、鸣声婉转而被笼养繁育
senses.example: The canary trilled from its brass cage by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 金丝雀在窗边的黄铜鸟笼里婉转啼鸣。
senses.why: The word began as the place name: the bird is named after its island home.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是地名：这种鸟以它的原产岛屿命名。

senses.title: A warning signal sensitive to danger
senses.definition: a person, animal, or indicator whose visible reaction gives early warning of hidden danger
senses.definitionCN: 以明显反应率先暴露隐性危险的人、动物或指标
senses.example: Coral reefs are the canary in the coal mine for ocean health.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁是海洋健康状况的预警金丝雀。
senses.why: Miners literally carried canaries into coal mines because the birds collapsed before humans did.
senses.whyCN: 矿工真的曾把金丝雀带进煤矿，因为鸟比人先倒下，可作预警。

senses.title: A light yellow color
senses.definition: a bright, light yellow like the bird's feathers
senses.definitionCN: 像这种鸟羽毛一样的明亮浅黄色
senses.example: She painted the kitchen canary yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 她把厨房刷成了金丝雀黄。
senses.why: The bird's name colors everything that shares its yellow.
senses.whyCN: 鸟名把这种黄色辐射给了所有同色的东西。

senses.title: An informer
senses.definition: slang for someone who betrays secrets to the authorities, from the bird's constant singing
senses.definitionCN: 俚语，指向当局出卖秘密的人，取自这种鸟不停歌唱的特性
senses.example: The gang discovered a canary in their ranks.
senses.exampleCN: 团伙发现自己内部出了告密者。
senses.why: A bird that never stops singing is a perfect image for someone who cannot keep quiet.
senses.whyCN: 一只叫个不停的鸟，正是「守不住嘴的人」的完美意象。

intro.en: Canary is the bird named after the Canary Islands, whose Latin name refers not to songbirds but to dogs.
intro.cn: canary 是以加那利群岛命名的鸟，而群岛的拉丁名指的并不是鸣禽，而是狗。

items.en: The root *ḱwṓn, dog, runs through the whole Indo-European dog-word family.
items.cn: 词根 *ḱwṓn（狗）贯穿整个印欧语系的「狗」词族。

items.en: Latin canarius meant of dogs, and Insulae Canariae, the Islands of the Dogs, was the Roman name for the archipelago.
items.cn: 拉丁语 canarius 意为「与狗有关的」，罗马人称该群岛为 Insulae Canariae（狗之群岛）。

items.en: Iberian sailors rendered the island name as Canaria and applied canario to the islands' small birds.
items.cn: 伊比利亚水手把岛名转写为 Canaria，并把 canario 用到群岛上的小型鸟类。

items.en: English canary bird first named the bird in the sixteenth century, later shortened to canary.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语先以 canary bird 称呼此鸟，后简化为 canary。

items.en: The yellow color sense appeared in the seventeenth century, applied to wine and cloth from the islands.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现黄色义，先用于群岛产的葡萄酒和布料。

items.en: The coal-mine warning practice gave the figurative sense, and American slang added the informer sense.
items.cn: 矿井预警的实践催生比喻义，美国俚语又添了告密者义。

note.en: Canary shares its dog root with a small word family and is easy to tangle with similarly spelled bird names.
note.cn: canary 的「狗」词根衍生出一小组词族，且容易与拼写相近的鸟类名混淆。

entries.definition: Of or like a dog, from the same Latin canis root.
entries.definitionCN: 犬的；犬齿，同出拉丁语 canis 词根。

entries.definition: A doghouse, from French chenil, ultimately the same dog root.
entries.definitionCN: 狗窝，经法语 chenil 上溯到同一「狗」词根。

entries.definition: A factory for canning food; only one letter from canary but from can.
entries.definitionCN: 罐头厂，与 canary 仅差一个字母，但源自 can（罐）。

entries.definition: A small open sandwich; spelled close but from a couch root.
entries.definitionCN: 小开胃点心，拼写相近但源自「沙发」一词根。

entries.definition: The bird family the canary belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 雀科，canary 所属的鸟类家族。

entries.definition: A guard or watcher that gives warning, the human figure of the canary role.
entries.definitionCN: 哨兵、守望者，是 canary 预警角色的人格化版本。

entries.definition: A leading indicator of trends, figurative like the mine canary.
entries.definitionCN: 领头羊、风向标，与矿井金丝雀同为比喻性指标。

entries.definition: One who betrays secrets, the plain word behind the slang sense.
entries.definitionCN: 告密者，是俚语义项背后的平实用词。

entries.definition: In political metaphor, the aggressive opposite of the small, warning songbird.
entries.definitionCN: 政治隐喻中的鹰派，与示警的小鸣禽形成象征性对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the island-of-dogs origin and the mine-shaft image.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「狗之群岛」词源与矿井画面的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Place first: Canary Islands, from Latin Insulae Canariae, the Islands of the Dogs.
normal.cn: 地名在先：加那利群岛源自拉丁语 Insulae Canariae（狗之群岛）。

normal.en: Same root: canary, canine, and kennel all descend from the dog word canis.
normal.cn: 同根记忆：canary、canine、kennel 都出自「狗」词 canis。

normal.en: Metaphor: a canary in a coal mine is the fixed phrase for an early-warning indicator.
normal.cn: 比喻义：固定说法「a canary in a coal mine」即「早期预警指标」。

normal.en: Color: canary yellow is the standard name for bright light yellow in fashion and design.
normal.cn: 颜色：canary yellow 是时尚与设计中明亮浅黄的标准色名。

normal.en: Slang hook: sing like a canary, to confess everything, links the bird's song to betrayal.
normal.cn: 俚语钩子：sing like a canary（全盘招供）把鸟鸣与告密连在一起。

abstract.en: A tiny yellow bird going quiet in the dark: everyone's alarm bell with feathers.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中一只突然噤声的小黄鸟：长着羽毛的警报器。

abstract.en: A swell of yellow paint across a gray wall, the room suddenly singing.
abstract.cn: 一抹淡黄刷过灰墙，整个房间顿时唱起歌来。

abstract.en: Dogs on a wild beach, named forever into an island, then into a bird.
abstract.cn: 野滩上的狗群：名字永远留给了岛，又从岛转给了鸟。

examples.en: Rising insurance claims were the canary that warned of the building's structural trouble.
examples.cn: 保险索赔的上升是预警这栋楼结构隐患的金丝雀。

examples.en: He kept a canary that sang every morning outside his studio.
examples.cn: 他养了一只金丝雀，每天清晨在画室外鸣唱。

examples.en: Under pressure, the suspect sang like a canary.
examples.cn: 在压力之下，嫌疑人对一切都招供了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克内瑞」——笼子可（克）内部（内）日日（瑞）有歌声，说的就是笼养的金丝雀；联想煤井里的小黄鸟一停叫大家就撤，淡黄色的小身躯格外醒目。

root: 以地名 Canary Islands（加那利群岛）命名；岛名出自拉丁语 Insulae Canariae（狗之群岛，因岛上多大型野狗），词根为拉丁语 canis（狗），可上溯至印欧词根 *ḱwṓn。因此「金丝雀」其实是「狗之鸟」，与 canine（犬的）同根。俚语「告密者」由其不停鸣唱的特征引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From the island-named songbird the word grows into an early-warning metaphor, a color name, and slang for an informer.
sensesIntro.cn: 从以岛命名的鸣禽出发，词义生长为预警的比喻、颜色名称以及指告密者的俚语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small yellow bird whose song and silence both carry messages.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只淡黄小鸟，它的歌声与沉默都传递着讯息。

branches.en: THE CAGE: the literal finch bred for color and song.
branches.cn: 鸟笼：字面义的雀鸟，为羽色与歌声而繁育。

branches.en: THE MINE: the bird that collapses first and saves the miners.
branches.cn: 矿井：先倒下却救了矿工的鸟。

branches.en: THE PAINTBOX: the yellow that borrowed the bird's name.
branches.cn: 颜料盒：借走鸟名的黄色。

branches.en: THE INTERROGATION: the singer who cannot keep quiet.
branches.cn: 审讯室：守不住嘴的歌唱者。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: both senses turn the bird's voice into information others must heed.
branches.cn: 讯息：两个义项都把鸟鸣转译成他人必须重视的信息。

intro.en: Canary is a place-name turned common noun; its derivational life sits in compounds and the dog-root family.
intro.cn: canary 是由地名转成的普通名词；其派生活动体现在复合词与「狗」词根家族中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root canis, dog, extends far beyond the bird into anatomy and everyday dog words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 canis（狗）的延伸远不止这只鸟，还进入解剖学和日常犬类词汇。

items.example: Canis familiaris, the species name of the dog
items.exampleCN: Canis familiaris，狗的物种学名。

items.example: Insulae Canariae
items.exampleCN: 狗之群岛（加那利群岛的拉丁名）。

items.meaning: noun-forming ending in the borrowed bird name
items.meaningCN: 借入鸟名中的名词性词尾
items.example: canary from canario
items.exampleCN: canary 由西班牙语 canario 转来。

items.example: a canary yellow raincoat
items.exampleCN: 一件金丝雀黄的雨衣。

items.meaning: a grass native to the Canary region
items.meaningCN: 草芦（原产加那利地区的草）
items.example: canary grass seed for birds
items.exampleCN: 喂鸟用的草芦籽。

items.example: canine teeth
items.exampleCN: 犬齿。

items.structure: French doublet of the same root
items.example: the dog sleeps in its kennel
items.exampleCN: 狗睡在窝里。

items.example: He sang like a canary at the trial.
items.exampleCN: 他在庭上竹筒倒豆子般招了供。

definition_zh: 树的；长于树上的；栖于树的
definition_en: relating to trees; living in trees
core_image: 树冠间的居民：猴子抓住枝条荡过头顶的绿海
scene: 雨林向导压低声音，指向树冠间晃动的黑影。 The arboreal monkeys leapt from branch to branch above us.
sceneCN: 这里 arboreal 是「栖于树的」（第 2 个义项：以树为家的动物）；句意为：树栖的猴子在我们头顶从一根枝条跃向另一根。

pos.zh: 树的；栖于树的；长在树上的

derivatives.zh: 词根名词，义为「凉亭；（古）树」

senses.title: Relating to trees
senses.definition: of or connected with trees in general
senses.definitionCN: 与树木总体相关的
senses.example: The valley is famous for its arboreal landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山谷以满目林木著称。
senses.why: The Latin arbor means tree, so anything tree-flavored takes the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arbor 意为树，凡带树味之物都可用这个形容词。

senses.title: Living in trees
senses.definition: describing animals that live mainly in trees
senses.definitionCN: 形容主要在树上生活的动物
senses.example: Sloths are slow arboreal mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 树懒是行动缓慢的树栖哺乳动物。
senses.why: The tree becomes a home, not just a plant.
senses.whyCN: 树不仅是植物，更是家园。

senses.title: Growing on trees
senses.definition: describing plants or organs that grow upon trees
senses.definitionCN: 形容附生或生长于树上的植物或器官
senses.example: Some orchids are arboreal, rooting in bark.
senses.exampleCN: 有些兰花是附生的，扎根于树皮。
senses.why: Trees can also be the soil for other life.
senses.whyCN: 树也可以成为其他生命的土壤。

senses.title: Shaped for tree life
senses.definition: describing bodies or limbs adapted to climbing and balance in trees
senses.definitionCN: 形容为攀爬与树上平衡而演化的身体或四肢
senses.example: Its arboreal hands can grip thin branches.
senses.exampleCN: 它那双适于树栖的手能抓住细枝。
senses.why: Living above ground remodels the body.
senses.whyCN: 在树上生活重塑了身体。

senses.title: Dominated by trees
senses.definition: describing regions or ecosystems where trees dominate
senses.definitionCN: 形容树木占主导的地区或生态系统
senses.example: The arboreal zone begins above the shrubs.
senses.exampleCN: 乔木带从灌木带之上开始。
senses.why: Where trees rule, the landscape takes their name.
senses.whyCN: 树木称王之处，景观便以树为名。

senses.title: Resembling a tree
senses.definition: branching or spreading like a tree
senses.definitionCN: 像树一样分叉或铺展
senses.example: Lightning left an arboreal scar on the trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 闪电在树干上留下树状的疤痕。
senses.why: The branching form is the tree's signature.
senses.whyCN: 分叉之形是树的签名。

senses.title: Elevated or lofty by metaphor
senses.definition: figuratively high up, detached from the ground level
senses.definitionCN: 比喻居高、脱离地面的
senses.example: His arboreal view of the problem ignored street realities.
senses.exampleCN: 他对问题的俯瞰视角忽视了街头的现实。
senses.why: Height in the tree maps to distance from ordinary life.
senses.whyCN: 树上的高度映射为对日常生活的距离感。

senses.title: In scientific classification
senses.definition: a technical term distinguishing tree-living habits in biology
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中区分树栖习性的术语
senses.example: Field notes classified the lemur as arboreal.
senses.exampleCN: 野外记录把这只狐猴归类为树栖动物。
senses.why: Learned Latin roots give science its labels.
senses.whyCN: 学术性的拉丁词根为科学提供标签。

intro.en: Arboreal comes from Latin arbor, tree, plus the adjective suffix -alis, via the form arboreus.
intro.cn: arboreal 来自拉丁语 arbor（树）加形容词后缀 -alis，经 arboreus 一形传入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *h3erb- denoted plants or produce.
items.cn: 重构词根 *h3erb- 指植物、出产。

items.en: Arbor meant a tree, set against shrubs and herbs.
items.cn: arbor 意为乔木，与灌木、草本相对。

items.en: Arboreus meant of a tree or tree-like.
items.cn: arboreus 意为树的、似树的。

items.en: English borrowed arboreal in the seventeenth century for tree-related things.
items.cn: 英语十七世纪借入 arboreal，指与树相关之物。

items.en: Biology fixed it as the standard term for tree-dwelling life.
items.cn: 生物学将其固定为树栖生物的标准术语。

note.en: Arboreal belongs to the arbor family and stands opposite ground-dwelling terms.
note.cn: arboreal 属于 arbor 词族，与陆栖类词相对。

entries.definitionCN: 藤架凉亭；（古）树

entries.definition: a garden where trees are grown and studied

entries.definition: a specialist in the care of trees

normalIntro.cn: 把 arboreal 挂到 arbor 这棵树上，词族便自行生长。

normal.en: arboreal = arbor (tree) + -eal (relating to): tree-related.
normal.cn: arboreal = arbor（树）+ -eal（相关）：与树相关的。

normal.en: Biology anchor: arboreal versus terrestrial species.
normal.cn: 生物锚点：树栖种 vs 陆栖种。

normal.en: Family: arbor, arborist, arboretum, arboreal.
normal.cn: 词族：arbor、arborist、arboretum、arboreal。

normal.en: Image anchor: monkeys swinging through the canopy.
normal.cn: 意象锚点：猴子在林冠间荡跃。

normal.en: Orchid note: some plants are arboreal too, growing on bark.
normal.cn: 补记：有些植物也附生树上，扎根树皮。

abstract.en: An apartment building made of branches, full of animal tenants.
abstract.cn: 一座树枝造的公寓楼，住满动物房客。

abstract.en: An escalator of vines lifting life into the canopy.
abstract.cn: 一架藤蔓扶梯，把生命送上林冠。

abstract.en: Arboreal sounds like 'our bowl real': our bowl of soup grew on a real tree.
abstract.cn: arboreal 听着像 our-bowl-real：我们那碗汤长在真树上。

examples.en: Owls are partly arboreal hunters.
examples.cn: 猫头鹰部分属于树栖猎手。

examples.en: The island's arboreal wildlife draws researchers yearly.
examples.cn: 岛上的树栖野生动物每年吸引研究者前来。

examples.en: Arboreal roots crack old walls in the tropics.
examples.cn: 在热带，附生树的根系会撑裂老墙。

sensesIntro.en: From the Latin tree, arboreal extends to tree-related landscapes, tree-dwelling animals, plants growing on trees, bodies shaped for climbing, tree-dominated zones, tree-like forms, figurative height, and scientific labeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拉丁语「树」出发，arboreal 延伸到林木景观、树栖动物、附生植物、攀爬体形、乔木地带、树状形态、比喻的高踞与科学分类标签。

core.cn: 核心意象：在地面之上的绿色世界里的生活

branches.cn: 树即景观与主导

definition_zh: 爬行动物；爬虫；（贬义）卑劣的人
definition_en: a cold-blooded vertebrate with scales that lays eggs on land, such as a snake, lizard or turtle, or a contemptible person
core_image: 一只蜥蜴腹部几乎贴地，四肢向两侧撑开，在热石上缓缓前行
scene: 沙漠的岩石上，一只蜥蜴腹部贴地，四肢向两侧撑开，慢慢向前爬。 The reptile moved low over the hot stone, its belly almost touching the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 reptile 指「爬行动物」（第 1 个义项：体表有鳞、在陆上产卵的变温脊椎动物）；句意为这只爬行动物贴着滚烫的石头低身前行，腹部几乎碰到地面。

pos.zh: 爬行动物；爬虫
卑劣的人（贬义，旧用法）

derivatives.zh: 爬行动物的；像爬行动物的

senses.title: A scaly, cold-blooded vertebrate
senses.titleCN: 体表有鳞的变温脊椎动物
senses.definition: a vertebrate with dry scaly skin that regulates its body temperature by behaviour and usually lays eggs on land
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤干燥有鳞、靠行为调节体温、通常在陆上产卵的脊椎动物
senses.example: The reptile moved low over the hot stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这只爬行动物贴着热石低身前行。
senses.why: The Latin name means 'creeping thing', and the defining traits are scales and a body that must warm itself in the sun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原名意为「爬行的东西」，其标志特征是鳞片与必须靠晒太阳取暖的身体。

senses.title: The class Reptilia as a whole
senses.definition: the reptiles collectively, a vertebrate class that in modern classification includes birds
senses.definitionCN: 所有爬行动物的集合，现代分类中这一纲还包括鸟类
senses.example: Reptiles occupy every continent except Antarctica.
senses.exampleCN: 除南极洲外，每个大陆都有爬行动物。
senses.why: Because the class is a formal unit, the plural often names a category rather than individual animals.
senses.whyCN: 因为这是一个正式分类单元，复数常指范畴而不是个体动物。

senses.title: A reptile kept as a pet
senses.titleCN: 作为宠物饲养的爬行动物
senses.definition: a snake, lizard or turtle kept in a terrarium and sold through the pet trade
senses.definitionCN: 养在饲养箱中、经宠物贸易出售的蛇、蜥蜴或龟
senses.example: The shop sells reptile supplies as well as the animals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店既卖爬行动物，也卖饲养用品。
senses.why: The pet trade uses the class name as a market category, so reptile becomes a product label.
senses.whyCN: 宠物贸易把纲名当作市场类别，于是 reptile 成了产品标签。

senses.title: A venomous reptile
senses.definition: a reptile that injects venom through fangs or a sting, such as a viper
senses.definitionCN: 通过毒牙或毒刺注入毒液的爬行动物，如蝰蛇
senses.example: Antivenom is made from the venom of a reptile.
senses.exampleCN: 抗蛇毒血清由某种爬行动物的毒液制成。
senses.why: Medical writing uses the class name because the bite may come from a snake, a lizard or a turtle.
senses.whyCN: 医学文献用纲名，因为咬伤可能来自蛇、蜥蜴或龟。

senses.title: A fossil reptile
senses.definition: ancient reptile remains, including dinosaurs in traditional usage
senses.definitionCN: 古代爬行动物遗骸，传统用法中也包括恐龙
senses.example: The fossil reptile had a sail-like crest on its back.
senses.exampleCN: 这只爬行动物化石背部有帆状脊冠。
senses.why: Palaeontology long treated dinosaurs as reptiles, and the word still carries that history even though birds are their descendants.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学长期把恐龙当作爬行动物，这个词仍带着这段历史，尽管鸟类是恐龙的后代。

senses.title: The reptile house in a zoo
senses.definition: a heated building where snakes and other reptiles are displayed to the public
senses.definitionCN: 向公众展示蛇类等爬行动物、保持加热的馆舍
senses.example: The children queued for the reptile house.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排队等着进爬行动物馆。
senses.why: Zoos needed a short exhibit label, and the class name became a building name.
senses.whyCN: 动物园需要简短的展区名称，纲名于是成了建筑名。

senses.title: A contemptible person
senses.definition: an insulting term for someone seen as low, treacherous or grovelling
senses.definitionCN: 蔑称，指低劣、阴险或谄媚的人
senses.example: The old pamphlet called the informer a reptile.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧小册子把告密者称为卑劣之徒。
senses.why: The insult draws on the animal's belly-down movement and its reputation for coldness, turning 'creeping' into moral contempt.
senses.whyCN: 这个骂法利用了动物贴地爬行的姿态与「冷血」的名声，把「爬」转成道德上的轻蔑。

senses.title: Reptile leather
senses.definition: the skin of a snake, crocodile or other reptile used for bags, belts and shoes
senses.definitionCN: 用于包、带、鞋的蛇、鳄等爬行动物皮革
senses.example: The belt was made of reptile skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这条腰带是爬行动物皮革做的。
senses.why: The material trade names the product by its source class, so reptile also functions as an attributive noun.
senses.whyCN: 材料行业按来源类群给产品命名，因此 reptile 也作定语名词使用。

intro.en: Reptile goes back to Latin repere 'to creep' through the adjective reptilis; the name describes how the animal moves, not how it is built. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reptile 经形容词 reptilis 上溯到拉丁 repere「爬行」；这个名字描述的是行动方式，而非身体构造。年代均为约数。

items.en: Repere meant 'to creep, crawl'. Its deeper origin is not settled, so any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: repere 意为「爬行、匍匐」。其更深来源没有定论，凡为它提出的印欧词根都属重构。

items.en: Reptilis meant 'creeping, crawling', an adjective formed from the verb and used of animals that move close to the ground.
items.cn: reptilis 意为「爬行的、匍匐的」，由动词构成的形容词，用于贴地移动的动物。

items.en: English reptile is recorded from the late fourteenth century, first for creeping animals in general and later for the scaly vertebrate class.
items.cn: 英语 reptile 自 14 世纪后期有记录，最初泛指爬行动物，后来才专指有鳞的脊椎动物纲。

items.en: Eighteenth-century zoology fixed Reptilia as a class, separating snakes, lizards and turtles from amphibians and insects.
items.cn: 18 世纪动物学把 Reptilia 固定为一个纲，把蛇、蜥蜴、龟与两栖动物及昆虫分开。

items.en: From the eighteenth century 'reptile' was used as an insult for a low or grovelling person, drawing on the belly-down image.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，reptile 被用作侮辱语，指低劣或谄媚的人，取「贴地爬行」的形象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Latin stages are clear, but the pre-Latin origin of repere is unsettled and the exact first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：拉丁阶段清楚，但 repere 的拉丁语之前来源没有定论，英语确切首见书证也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same reptile stock; group two holds animal names and adjectives that are often misplaced around reptiles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 reptile 词族的形式；第二组是常被误置于爬行动物语境中的动物名与形容词。

entries.definition: Of or like reptiles; as a noun in science fiction it also means a reptile-like being.
entries.definitionCN: 爬行动物的或像爬行动物的；在科幻作品中作名词还指似爬行类的人形生物。

entries.definition: The formal Latin class name; Reptilia is the whole class, a reptile is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 正式拉丁纲名；Reptilia 是整个纲，reptile 是一个成员。

entries.definition: A botanical adjective meaning creeping along the ground; it shares the Latin verb but describes plants.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学形容词，意为贴地匍匐；它同出拉丁动词，却描述植物。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', it describes a reptile-like form without claiming it belongs to the class.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，描述似爬行动物的形态，并不表示它属于该纲。

entries.definition: A vertebrate that usually breeds in water and has moist skin; it is not a reptile, though both are cold-blooded.
entries.definitionCN: 通常在水中繁殖、皮肤潮湿的脊椎动物；它不是爬行动物，尽管两者都是变温动物。

entries.definition: A small reptile with four legs and a long tail; it is one kind of reptile, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 有四足和长尾的小型爬行动物；它是爬行动物的一种，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A limbless reptile; again a member of the class rather than a general term.
entries.definitionCN: 无肢的爬行动物；同样是纲内成员，而不是泛称。

entries.definition: An animal that relies on external heat; reptiles are ectotherms, but so are many fish and invertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖外部热量的动物；爬行动物是变温动物，但许多鱼与无脊椎动物也是。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Reptile comes from 'to creep': the animal that moves with its belly near the ground.
normal.cn: reptile 来自「爬行」：腹部贴近地面移动的动物。

normal.en: Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles are reptiles; frogs are amphibians.
normal.cn: 蛇、蜥蜴、龟、鳄是爬行动物；蛙是两栖动物。

normal.en: Reptilia is the class; reptile is one member; reptilian is the adjective.
normal.cn: Reptilia 是纲；reptile 是成员；reptilian 是形容词。

normal.en: Reptile house is the fixed zoo label for the heated exhibit building.
normal.cn: reptile house 是动物园里指加热展馆的固定说法。

normal.en: The insult 'reptile' plays on the same belly-down image, not on the biology.
normal.cn: 骂人的 reptile 用的是同一个「贴地」形象，与生物学无关。

abstract.en: Picture a body that must borrow its warmth from a stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一具必须向石头借温暖的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a creature that hears the ground through its jaw.
