definition_zh: 反驳；否认；与……相矛盾；自相矛盾
definition_en: to say the opposite of what someone has said, or to be inconsistent with something else
core_image: 两支箭头从同一点射出，指向完全相反的两个方向
scene: 法庭上，证人先说是九点，随后又改口说是十一点。律师说： You just contradicted your earlier statement.
sceneCN: 这里 contradict 是「反驳、自相矛盾」（第 1 个义项：说出相反的话）；句意：你刚刚与先前的陈述自相矛盾。

pos.zh: 反驳；否认；与……相矛盾
自相矛盾；说法不一致

derivatives.zh: 反驳者；提出相反说法的人

senses.title: Say the opposite of what someone said
senses.titleCN: 反驳：把对方的话反过来说
senses.definition: to state that what someone has just said is wrong, and give the opposite account
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人刚说的话是错的，并给出相反的说法
senses.example: She contradicted him in front of the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她当着整个委员会的面反驳了他。
senses.why: Latin contra dicere is literally 'to speak against'. The word does not merely disagree; it places a second statement directly opposite the first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 contra dicere 字面就是“反着说”。这个词不只是不同意，而是把第二句话直接放在第一句话的对面。

senses.title: Of statements: be inconsistent
senses.titleCN: 相互矛盾：两句话不能同时成立
senses.definition: of two statements or facts, to be incompatible so that both cannot be true at once
senses.definitionCN: （两句话或两个事实）互不相容，不能同时为真
senses.example: The two reports contradict each other on the date.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告在日期上互相矛盾。
senses.why: When two statements are set opposite each other, there is no ground on which both can stand. This 'be inconsistent with' sense is recorded from about 1600.
senses.whyCN: 当两句话被放到彼此对面，就没有任何一块地面能让两者同时站住。这一“与……不一致”义约记录于 1600 年。

senses.title: Deny a claim or an accusation
senses.definition: to deny the truth of a claim, accusation or rumour
senses.definitionCN: 否认某项主张、指控或传闻的真实性
senses.example: The company contradicted the rumour of a merger.
senses.exampleCN: 公司否认了合并的传闻。
senses.why: The sense 'deny the words or assertions of' is recorded from about 1600. Denial is the negative half of speaking against.
senses.whyCN: “否认某人的话或断言”这一义项约记录于 1600 年。否认是“反着说”的否定那一半。

senses.title: Contradict oneself
senses.titleCN: 自相矛盾：自己前后打起来
senses.definition: to make two statements that cannot both be true, so that one cancels the other
senses.definitionCN: 说出两句不能同时为真的话，使一句抵消另一句
senses.example: He contradicted himself twice during the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他在采访中两次自相矛盾。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the opposition inward: the speaker is now both parties, and the two statements pull against each other inside one mouth.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把对立转向内部：说话者现在同时是两方，两句话在同一张嘴里面互相拉扯。

senses.title: Contradictory: mutually opposed
senses.definition: the adjective describes two things that cannot both be true or both be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 形容词描述两件不能同时为真或同时被接受的事
senses.example: The witness gave two contradictory accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 证人给出了两份相互矛盾的陈述。
senses.why: The -ory suffix marks a relation of opposition: each item points away from the other, like the two arrows from one point.
senses.whyCN: -ory 后缀标记对立关系：两项各自背离对方，就像从同一点射出的两支反向箭头。

senses.title: Contradiction: the opposing statement
senses.definition: the noun for a statement that denies or opposes another statement
senses.definitionCN: 指否定或反对另一句话的那句陈述
senses.example: His calm reply was a contradiction of everything she had said.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的回答是对她所说一切的否定。
senses.why: The -tion noun names the second statement itself. In logic it is the proposition that asserts the negation of another.
senses.whyCN: -tion 名词命名第二句话本身。在逻辑中，它就是断言另一命题之否定的那个命题。

senses.title: Contradiction in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑矛盾：同时肯定与否
senses.definition: in logic, the relation between a statement and its negation, which cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中一个命题与其否定之间的关系，两者不能同时为真
senses.example: The proof ends in a contradiction, so the assumption is false.
senses.exampleCN: 证明以矛盾收尾，所以那个假设是假的。
senses.why: Philosophy uses contradiction as a tool: if assuming P leads to P and not-P, then P must be rejected. Two arrows cannot both be the true direction.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把矛盾当作工具：若假设 P 会推出 P 与非 P，则 P 必须被否定。两支箭头不可能同时是正确方向。

senses.title: Contradict the evidence or the record
senses.definition: of a fact or statement, to be contrary to what the evidence or record shows
senses.definitionCN: （事实或陈述）与证据或记录所显示的内容相反
senses.example: His version of events contradicts the phone records.
senses.exampleCN: 他对事件的描述与通话记录相矛盾。
senses.why: Here the second party is not a person but a record. The record 'speaks' too, and the verb treats it as an opposing voice.
senses.whyCN: 这里的第二方不是人，而是一份记录。记录也会“说话”，动词把它当成一个对立的声音。

senses.title: Contradict the trend or expectation
senses.definition: to be contrary to a general pattern, expectation or rule, often surprisingly
senses.definitionCN: 与一般模式、预期或规则相反，常含出人意料之意
senses.example: The results contradict the usual pattern of growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这些结果与通常的增长模式相反。
senses.why: This extension drops the human speaker entirely: any fact can stand opposite a pattern, and the pattern is what is contradicted.
senses.whyCN: 这一延伸完全去掉了人类说话者：任何事实都能站在某个模式对面，而被反驳的是那个模式。

intro.en: Contradict comes from Latin contradicere, in classical Latin two words: contra 'against' + dicere 'to say, speak'. It is literally 'speak against', and its relatives dictation, predict and verdict all keep the 'say' root.
intro.cn: contradict 来自拉丁语 contradicere，在古典拉丁语中是两个词：contra“反对”加 dicere“说、讲”。它字面就是“反着说”，其亲属 dictation、predict、verdict 都保留“说”这个词根。

items.en: Contra dicere meant 'to speak against'. The prefix contra was originally a comparative form meaning 'in comparison with', which hardened into 'against, opposite'.
items.cn: contra dicere 意为“反着说”。前缀 contra 最初是比较级形式，意为“与……相比”，后来固化为“反对、相反”。

items.en: Dicere 'to say, speak' comes from PIE *deik- 'to show, pronounce solemnly'. The same root gives dictate, predict, verdict, diction and index.
items.cn: dicere“说、讲”来自原始印欧语 *deik-“显示、郑重宣告”。同一词根给出 dictate、predict、verdict、diction、index。

items.en: English recorded contradict in the 1570s meaning 'speak against, oppose' — a sense now obsolete.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 70 年代记录 contradict，意为“反着说、反对”——这一义项现已废弃。

items.en: From the 1580s it meant 'assert the contrary or opposite of', which is the modern core.
items.cn: 自 16 世纪 80 年代起，它意为“断言相反或对立的一面”，这是现代的核心义。

items.en: Two senses appear around 1600: 'deny the words or assertions of' and, of statements, 'be inconsistent with'. The word moves from a person's speech to the relation between propositions.
items.cn: 约 1600 年出现两个义项：“否认某人的话或断言”，以及（就陈述而言）“与……不一致”。这个词从人的言语转向命题之间的关系。

items.en: Modern English keeps person-against-person (contradict a witness) and fact-against-fact (the data contradict the theory). Contradict is the only one of the con- verbs built on 'speak'.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留“人对人”（contradict a witness）与“事实对事实”（数据与理论相矛盾）。在 con- 系列动词里，contradict 是唯一建在“说”之上的。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the dicere root from two near-spellings; the near-meaning group ranks kinds of opposition from simple denial to logical refutation.
note.cn: 形近组把 dicere 词根与两个近形词分开；近义组按对立程度排列，从简单否认到逻辑反驳。

entries.definition: an agreement, or to shrink. Its root is trahere 'draw', so it means 'draw together', not 'speak against'.
entries.definitionCN: 协议，或收缩。它的词根是 trahere“拉”，所以是“拉到一起”，不是“反着说”。

entries.definition: to break a rule or law. Contra- 'against' + venire 'come' = come against, so it opposes a rule rather than a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则或法律。contra-“反对”加 venire“来”＝迎面而来，所以它反对的是规则，而不是陈述。

entries.definition: the way words are chosen and pronounced. It is the noun of dicere, the 'saying' side without contra-.
entries.definitionCN: 用词与发音的方式。它是 dicere 的名词，是“说”的一面，没有 contra-。

entries.definition: to state that something is not true. It is the simple negative act; contradict adds the opposing statement or the clash between two claims.
entries.definitionCN: 声称某事不真实。它是简单的否定行为；contradict 还加上“相反的说法”或“两种主张的冲突”。

entries.definition: to be against a plan, person or idea. It is broader and can be silent; contradict must be spoken or written.
entries.definitionCN: 反对计划、人或观念。它范围更广，可以不出声；contradict 必须说出或写出。

entries.definition: to prove a claim false with evidence. It is stronger than contradict, which only asserts the opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 用证据证明某主张为假。它比 contradict 更强，后者只是断言相反。

entries.definition: of facts, interests or statements, to be incompatible. It is the neutral verb for the clash, without the 'speaking' image.
entries.definitionCN: （事实、利益或陈述）互不相容。它是描述冲突的中性动词，没有“说话”的意象。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: contra 'against' + dicere 'say', the same-root family predict, dictate, verdict, diction, and the fixed phrase contradict oneself.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构件：contra“反对”+ dicere“说”，同根词族 predict、dictate、verdict、diction，以及固定搭配 contradict oneself。

normal.en: Contra means 'against' and dicere means 'say'. To contradict is simply to say against.
normal.cn: contra 意为“反对”，dicere 意为“说”。contradict 就是“反着说”。

normal.en: Predict is 'say before', dictate is 'say for writing', and verdict is 'truly said'. All keep the dic- root.
normal.cn: predict 是“提前说”，dictate 是“说给别人写”，verdict 是“如实说出”。它们都保留 dic- 词根。

normal.en: Contradict, contract and contact look alike but rest on three roots: speak against (dicere), draw together (trahere), touch (tangere).
normal.cn: contradict、contract、contact 形似但立足三个词根：反着说（dicere）、拉到一起（trahere）、触碰（tangere）。

normal.en: Contradict oneself is the same opposition turned inward: you are both the speaker and the one spoken against.
normal.cn: contradict oneself 是同一个对立转向内部：你既是说话者，也是被反驳的那个人。

normal.en: Contradictory is the adjective of two arrows; contradiction is the second arrow itself.
normal.cn: contradictory 是两支箭的形容词；contradiction 就是第二支箭本身。

abstract.en: Picture one point with two arrows leaving it in exactly opposite directions. Only one of them can point where the truth is.
abstract.cn: 想象一个点射出两支方向完全相反的箭。只有一支能指向真相所在的方向。

abstract.en: The arrows can be two people, two reports, a claim and a record, or a theory and its data.
abstract.cn: 这两支箭可以是两个人、两份报告、一项主张与一份记录，或一个理论与它的数据。

abstract.en: Because the word means 'speak against', even a silent record 'speaks' when it contradicts a claim; English lends a voice to the evidence.
abstract.cn: 因为这个词本义是“反着说”，所以连沉默的记录在与主张冲突时也“说话”；英语把声音借给了证据。

examples.en: She contradicted the official account of the accident.
examples.cn: 她反驳了官方对事故的说法。

examples.en: The two witnesses contradicted each other.
examples.cn: 两名证人彼此的说法相互矛盾。

examples.en: His actions contradict everything he says about saving money.
examples.cn: 他的行为与他关于省钱的言论完全矛盾。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯·戳·迪克特”——肯（定）戳（穿）迪克特（dict 说）的话，把它反过来讲 → contradict 反驳、矛盾

root: 源自拉丁语 contra dicere“反着说”，由 contra“反对”+ dicere“说”构成，核心是“把一句话放到另一句话的正对面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of contradict, all built on two arrows. A person, a rumour, one's own earlier words, a logical proposition, a record, an expectation — each can be placed opposite something that claims to be true.
sensesIntro.cn: contradict 的九个义项都建立在两支箭上。一个人、一则传闻、自己先前的话、一个逻辑命题、一份记录、一种预期——每一个都能被放到某个自称真实之物的对面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arrows leaving one point in exactly opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支箭从同一点射向完全相反的方向。

branches.en: SPEAKING AGAINST: a person denies or opposes what another has said, and the second voice is the answer.
branches.cn: 反着说：一个人否认或反对另一个人所说的话，第二个声音就是回答。

branches.en: FACTS AGAINST FACTS: two reports, or a version against a record — neither has a mouth, yet they clash.
branches.cn: 事实对事实：两份报告，或一种说法对一份记录——它们都没有嘴，却发生了冲突。

branches.en: TURNED INWARD: self-contradiction places both arrows inside one speaker.
branches.cn: 转向内部：自相矛盾把两支箭都放进同一个说话者体内。

branches.en: THE LOGICAL FORM: contradictory marks the relation, contradiction names the opposing statement, and logic uses it as a proof tool.
branches.cn: 逻辑形式：contradictory 标记关系，contradiction 命名那句相反的话，逻辑则把它当作证明工具。

branches.en: AGAINST THE EXPECTATION: a result can contradict the trend, standing out from the pattern everyone expected it to follow.
branches.cn: 与预期相反：一个结果可以与趋势相违，脱离众人预期它应遵循的模式。

intro.en: Contradict is contra- + dict- + -Ø. English adds -ion, -ory, -or and -able, and the broader dic- family keeps the 'say' meaning.
intro.cn: contradict 是 contra- + dict- + -Ø。英语加 -ion、-ory、-or、-able，而更广的 dic- 词族保留“说”的意义。

latinIntro.en: The Latin dicere family is very large: dicere, dictus 'said', contradictio, dictio 'a saying', praedicere 'foretell', and verdictum 'truly said'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere 词族非常庞大：dicere、dictus“说过的”、contradictio、dictio“说法”、praedicere“预言”、verdictum“如实说出”。

items.meaning: to speak against; to be inconsistent with
items.example: He contradicted the witness calmly.
items.exampleCN: 他平静地反驳了证人。

items.meaning: a statement that opposes another; the state of clashing
items.meaningCN: 矛盾；反驳；矛盾之处（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: There is a contradiction between the two clauses.
items.exampleCN: 两个条款之间存在矛盾。

items.meaning: mutually opposed; unable to be true together
items.meaningCN: 相互矛盾的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The witness gave contradictory answers.
items.exampleCN: 证人给出了相互矛盾的回答。

items.meaning: a person who contradicts or opposes
items.example: His main contradictor was the junior minister.
items.exampleCN: 他主要的反驳者是那位副部长。

items.meaning: able to be contradicted or denied
items.meaningCN: 可被反驳的（-able 表可能）
items.example: That claim is not easily contradictable.
items.exampleCN: 那个主张不容易被反驳。

items.meaning: the state of contradicting one's own words
items.example: The memo is a self-contradiction.
items.exampleCN: 这份备忘录自相矛盾。

items.meaning: to say what will happen before it happens
items.meaningCN: 预测；预言（pre- 表之前，同一词根）
items.example: Scientists predict a rise in sea level.
items.exampleCN: 科学家预测海平面会上升。

items.meaning: to say words for someone to write; to give orders
items.example: She dictated the letter to her assistant.
items.exampleCN: 她向助理口述了这封信。

items.meaning: the decision a jury gives, literally 'truly said'
items.meaningCN: 裁决（字面“如实说出”，同一词根）
items.example: The jury reached a verdict at noon.
items.exampleCN: 陪审团中午作出了裁决。

items.meaning: the choice and use of words; pronunciation
items.example: The poem's diction is deliberately old-fashioned.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗的措辞刻意古旧。

definition_zh: 流沙；[喻] 让人越陷越深的处境；陷阱
definition_en: loose wet sand that swallows what rests on it, or a situation that traps a person
core_image: 一只脚踩上看似结实的地面，地面却开始把脚往下吸
scene: 向导喊住队伍，说那片看着平坦的沙地其实是流沙。 The guide stopped the group and warned that the flat stretch ahead was quicksand.
sceneCN: 这里 quicksand 指流沙（第 1 个义项：会下沉的沙地）；句意为向导喊住队伍，说那片看着平坦的沙地其实是流沙。

pos.zh: 流沙；让人越陷越深的处境；陷阱

senses.title: A patch of quicksand
senses.definition: wet sand that yields under weight and pulls things down
senses.definitionCN: 受重压就松动、把东西往下拉的湿沙
senses.example: The guide stopped the group and warned that the flat stretch ahead was quicksand.
senses.exampleCN: 向导喊住队伍，警告前方那片平坦的沙地是流沙。
senses.why: The first sense is geological and concrete.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是地质的、具体的。

senses.title: Sinking in quicksand
senses.definition: the experience of being drawn down faster the more one struggles
senses.definitionCN: 越挣扎被拉得越快的体验
senses.example: The more he struggled, the faster the quicksand took him.
senses.exampleCN: 他越挣扎，流沙把他吞得越快。
senses.why: The image carries a lesson about effort turned against itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象带着一条教训：力气反而与自己作对。

senses.title: A moral quicksand
senses.definition: a situation in which each attempt to escape makes the position worse
senses.definitionCN: 每一次脱身的尝试都让处境更糟的局面
senses.example: The committee found itself in moral quicksand over the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在这份合同上陷入了道德的流沙。
senses.why: The word moves from ground to conscience without losing its pull.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从地面移到良心，吸力没有丢。

senses.title: The quicksand of debt
senses.definition: a financial trap where borrowing to pay debt deepens it
senses.definitionCN: 靠借新债还旧债而越陷越深的财务陷阱
senses.example: Short-term loans became the quicksand of debt.
senses.exampleCN: 短期贷款变成了债务的流沙。
senses.why: Economics uses the image for a self-feeding cycle.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用这个意象指自我喂养的循环。

senses.title: A political quicksand
senses.definition: a controversy that consumes everyone who tries to settle it
senses.definitionCN: 会吞掉每个试图解决它的人的政治争议
senses.example: The minister stepped into political quicksand with one remark.
senses.exampleCN: 部长一句话就踏进了政治流沙。
senses.why: Public life borrows the ground that cannot hold weight.
senses.whyCN: 公共生活借用了这片承不住重量的地面。

senses.title: Quicksand as a trap
senses.definition: any trap that looks like solid ground until it is entered
senses.definitionCN: 任何在踏入之前都像坚实土地的陷阱
senses.example: The offer looked solid, but it was quicksand under a thin crust.
senses.exampleCN: 那个提议看起来坚实，其实薄壳之下就是流沙。
senses.why: The sense abstracts the deception, not the sand.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项抽象的是欺骗，而不是沙。

senses.title: A person who drags others down
senses.definition: someone whose problems pull everyone near them into the same pit
senses.definitionCN: 其问题把身边人都拖进同一个坑的人
senses.example: He was quicksand to every friend who tried to help.
senses.exampleCN: 对每个想帮他的朋友来说，他就是流沙。
senses.why: The metaphor can attach to a person, unusually.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻罕见地可以附着在人身上。

senses.title: Versus swamp
senses.definition: dry-looking sand that swallows, as opposed to open standing water
senses.definitionCN: 看似干燥却会吞人的沙，与敞开的积水相对
senses.example: A swamp is seen before it is entered; quicksand is not.
senses.exampleCN: 沼泽在踏入前就看得见，流沙却看不见。
senses.why: The pair separates the visible bog from the hidden one.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词把看得见的泥沼与看不见的分开。

intro.en: Quicksand joins quick, in its old sense 'living or moving', with sand.
intro.cn: quicksand 把 quick（古义为「活的、会动的」）与 sand 组合在一起。

items.en: Quick once meant alive or moving, as in the quick and the dead.
items.cn: quick 古义为活着的、会动的，如 the quick and the dead。

items.en: The compound named sand that moves like a living thing.
items.cn: 这个复合词指像活物一样会动的沙。

items.en: Sailors and mapmakers spread the warning word.
items.cn: 水手与制图者传播了这个警告词。

items.en: Novelists turned the sand into a metaphor for moral traps.
items.cn: 小说家把这种沙变成道德陷阱的比喻。

items.en: Today it names any situation that swallows effort.
items.cn: 今天它命名任何吞没努力的处境。

note.en: The look-alike group is the quick- family; the near-meaning group separates swamp, bog, mire and sinkhole.
note.cn: 形近组是 quick 词族；近义组把「沼泽」「泥炭沼」「泥潭」「天坑」分开。

entries.definition: fast, or formerly alive.
entries.definitionCN: 快的，或古义「活着的」。

entries.definition: to make faster or more alive.
entries.definitionCN: 加快或使更有生气。

entries.definition: the old name for mercury.
entries.definitionCN: 水银的旧称。

entries.definition: a hedge of living plants.
entries.definitionCN: 由活植物构成的树篱。

entries.definition: waterlogged ground with trees.
entries.definitionCN: 有树的积水地。

entries.definition: soft wet ground of decaying plants.
entries.definitionCN: 腐植形成的软湿地。

entries.definition: deep mud that holds the foot.
entries.definitionCN: 会吸住脚的深泥。

entries.definition: a hole formed by collapsed ground.
entries.definitionCN: 地面塌陷形成的洞。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of firm-looking ground that begins to pull a boot down.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「看似结实的地面开始把靴子往下吸」的画面。

normal.en: Quicksand is quick plus sand: sand that moves like something alive.
normal.cn: quicksand 是 quick 加 sand：像活物一样会动的沙。

normal.en: Picture a flat grey stretch that looks easier than the path.
normal.cn: 想象一片平坦的灰色地带，看起来比小路还好走。

normal.en: Say KWIK-sand; the first syllable is short and sharp.
normal.cn: 读 KWIK-sand，第一音节短而利。

normal.en: Struggling makes it worse: the image is about effort turned against itself.
normal.cn: 挣扎会让它更糟：这个意象讲的是力气反噬自己。

normal.en: The word always begins with a surface that lies.
normal.cn: 这个词总以一个说谎的表面开场。

abstract.en: Quicksand is a trap that rewards panic with speed.
abstract.cn: 流沙是一个用速度奖励恐慌的陷阱。

abstract.en: Every metaphor of quicksand is about a system that feeds on the attempt to escape.
abstract.cn: 每个流沙的比喻，都关于一个靠脱身尝试来喂养自己的系统。

abstract.en: The safest move is to spread weight and stop struggling, which is hard advice in any crisis.
abstract.cn: 最安全的做法是摊开重量、停止挣扎，这在任何危机里都是难听的忠告。

examples.en: The more he struggled, the faster the quicksand took him.
examples.cn: 他越挣扎，流沙把他吞得越快。

examples.en: Short-term loans became the quicksand of debt.
examples.cn: 短期贷款变成了债务的流沙。

examples.en: The offer looked solid, but it was quicksand under a thin crust.
examples.cn: 那个提议看起来坚实，其实薄壳之下就是流沙。

dict_mnemonic.text: quick（活的、会动）+ sand（沙）→ 会动的沙，流沙。

root: 英语 quick（古义「活的」）+ sand（沙）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses sink through one image: the sand itself, the sinking, a moral trap, a debt cycle, a political fight, deception, a person and the contrast with a visible swamp.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沉进同一个意象：沙本身、下沉、道德陷阱、债务循环、政治争斗、欺骗、一个人，以及与可见沼泽的对照。

branches.en: The sand and the experience of sinking.

branches.en: Moral and financial traps that feed themselves.
branches.cn: 自我喂养的道德与财务陷阱。

branches.en: Public controversy as ground that cannot hold.
branches.cn: 作为承不住重量的地面的公共争议。

branches.en: Deception itself and the person who spreads it.
branches.cn: 欺骗本身与传播它的人。

branches.en: The hidden trap set against the visible bog.
branches.cn: 隐藏的陷阱与可见的泥沼相对。

intro.en: The quick- family keeps the old sense of alive or moving: quicksand, quicksilver and quickset all describe something that seems to live.

latinIntro.cn: 两个部件都是朴素的英语；quick 可追到古英语 cwic（活着的），sand 就是沙，中间没有拉丁语层。

senses.title: An algebraic expression with two terms
senses.definition: a mathematical expression consisting of two terms connected by a plus or minus sign
senses.definitionCN: 由两个项以加号或减号连接的数学表达式
senses.example: The expression x plus y is the simplest binomial.
senses.exampleCN: 表达式 x 加 y 是最简单的二项式。
senses.why: Bi- means two and the -nomial part comes from nomen name; in algebra the two names are simply the two terms that the expression carries.
senses.whyCN: bi- 意为「二」，-nomial 部分来自 nomen「名字」；在代数里，这两个「名字」就是表达式所携带的两个项。

senses.title: A two-part biological name
senses.titleCN: 由两部分构成的生物学名
senses.definition: a scientific name made of a genus name followed by a species name
senses.definitionCN: 由属名加种名构成的学名
senses.example: Homo sapiens is a binomial that every biology student meets early.
senses.exampleCN: Homo sapiens 是每个生物学生很早就接触到的双名。
senses.why: Taxonomy gives each species two names joined into one label, so the mathematical word for two terms was borrowed for two name parts.
senses.whyCN: 分类学给每个物种两个名字并合成一个标签，于是数学里表示「两项」的词被借来表示「两个名称部分」。

senses.title: Consisting of two terms or names
senses.titleCN: 由两项或两个名称组成的
senses.definition: having or using two terms, names or parts
senses.definitionCN: 具有或使用两个项、名称或部分的
senses.example: The catalogue uses a binomial label for each species.
senses.exampleCN: 目录为每个物种使用一个双名标签。
senses.why: The adjective simply states the count: whatever the field, two elements are being joined into one unit.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是陈述数量：无论在哪个领域，都是把两个要素合成一个单位。

senses.title: A two-outcome statistical model
senses.titleCN: 只有两种结果的统计模型
senses.definition: describing a statistical experiment or distribution with exactly two possible outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 描述恰好有两种可能结果的统计实验或分布
senses.example: A coin toss is modelled as a binomial experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 抛硬币被建模为二项实验。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the two-part structure but applies it to outcomes: success or failure, heads or tails.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了「两部分」的结构，却把它用在结果上：成功或失败、正面或反面。

senses.title: The two-term polynomial as an object
senses.titleCN: 作为一个数学对象的二项多项式
senses.definition: a polynomial that contains exactly two terms
senses.definitionCN: 恰好含两个项的多项式
senses.example: In this chapter every binomial is written in descending powers.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一章里，每个二项式都按降幂书写。
senses.why: Used as a noun, the word points at the object itself rather than at its property of having two terms.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词指向对象本身，而不是它「有两个项」这一属性。

senses.title: A two-element combination in general
senses.titleCN: 泛指由两个要素构成的组合
senses.definition: a combination or pairing of exactly two elements
senses.definitionCN: 恰好由两个要素构成的组合或配对
senses.example: The study treats nature and nurture as a binomial, not as rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把先天与后天当作一个双项组合，而非对立的两方。
senses.why: Outside mathematics the word can label any paired structure, because the two-part frame is what the speaker wants to stress.
senses.whyCN: 在数学之外，这个词可标记任何成对结构，因为说话者要强调的正是「两部分」这个框架。

senses.title: A two-word compound expression
senses.titleCN: 由两个词构成的复合表达
senses.definition: a fixed expression built from two words that function as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 由两个词构成、整体起一个单位作用的固定表达
senses.example: The term red fox is a binomial in ordinary descriptive writing.
senses.exampleCN: “红狐”这一说法在普通描写文中是一个双词组合。
senses.why: Linguists borrow the word when a two-word label behaves like a single name, echoing the taxonomic pattern.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家借用这个词，是指一个双词标签像单个名称那样起作用，与分类学的模式相呼应。

senses.title: A Latin-form two-part name on a label
senses.titleCN: 标签上以拉丁形式书写的双名
senses.definition: the Latin-form two-part name printed on a specimen or collection label
senses.definitionCN: 印在标本或藏品标签上的拉丁形式双名
senses.example: The curator corrected the binomial on the label before the exhibition opened.
senses.exampleCN: 展览开幕前，馆员更正了标签上的双名。
senses.why: In museum work the abstract system turns into ink: a binomial is what you actually read on the little card.
senses.whyCN: 在博物馆工作中，抽象体系变成墨迹：双名就是你真正在那张小卡片上读到的东西。

intro.en: Binomial comes from Late Latin binomius having two names, built on bini two each and nomen name; the mathematical use spread through French in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: binomial 来自晚期拉丁 binomius「有两个名字」，由 bini「各两个」与 nomen「名字」构成；数学用法在 16 世纪经法语传播。

items.en: Bini meant two each or in pairs, from bis twice; it marks the count of two rather than the act of naming.
items.cn: bini 意为「各两个、成对」，来自 bis「两次」；它标记的是数量二，而不是命名动作。

items.en: Nomen meant name and supplies the second element; the same root appears in nomenclature and misnomer.
items.cn: nomen 意为「名字」，提供第二个成分；同一词根出现在 nomenclature 与 misnomer 中。

items.en: Bini plus nomen produced binomius, having two names, an adjective used for things described by a pair of terms.
items.cn: bini 加 nomen 构成 binomius「有两个名字的」，用于以两个词来描述的事物。

items.en: French binôme named the two-term algebraic expression in the sixteenth century, and English borrowed the word in the 1550s.
items.cn: 法语 binôme 在 16 世纪指含两个项的代数式，英语于 16 世纪中叶借入。

items.en: Biology later applied the same adjective to names in two parts, and binomial nomenclature became the standard phrase in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 生物学后来把同一形容词用于由两部分构成的名称，binomial nomenclature 在 19 世纪成为标准说法。

items.en: Source partly uncertain: the nomen root is clear, but some accounts derive the mathematical term from Greek nomos part rather than Latin nomen; that Greek link is a hypothesis, and the first date of the biological sense is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源部分不确定：nomen 词根清楚，但有些说法认为数学术语来自希腊 nomos「部分」而非拉丁 nomen；这一希腊语联系只是假说，生物义的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look alike because of the bi- prefix but descend from different roots; group two holds words close in meaning within algebra and naming.
note.cn: 第一组是因 bi- 前缀而形近、却来自不同词根的同形词；第二组是代数与命名范围内意思相近的词。

entries.definition: Bi- two plus annus year: happening every two years, so the bi- is shared but the root is annus, not nomen.
entries.definitionCN: bi-「二」加 annus「年」：每两年发生一次，因此 bi- 相同而词根是 annus，并非 nomen。

entries.definition: Bi- plus latus side: involving two sides, which shows the same prefix over a different root.
entries.definitionCN: bi- 加 latus「边」：涉及两侧，说明同一前缀可接不同词根。

entries.definition: From Latin binarius of two: made of two parts or using two digits; it is closer in sense to binomial than to nomen words.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 binarius「二的」：由两部分构成或使用两个数字；在语义上比 nomen 词族更接近 binomial。

entries.definition: A later variant of binomial used mainly in biology for two-part names; the two forms differ in spelling, not in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: binomial 的后起异体，主要用于生物学的双名；两种形式只差拼写，意义相同。

entries.definition: The three-term counterpart of a binomial, built with tri- three; naming follows the same pattern.
entries.definitionCN: binomial 的三项对应词，由 tri-「三」构成；构词方式相同。

entries.definition: An expression with a single term; it marks the lower end of the same series.
entries.definitionCN: 只含一个项的表达式；它标出同一序列的下限。

entries.definition: An expression with one or more terms, of which a binomial is the special case with exactly two.
entries.definitionCN: 含一个或多个项的表达式，二项式是其中恰好两项的特例。

entries.definition: The formal two-part name of an organism; it is what a binomial denotes in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 生物正式的两部分名称；在生物学中正是 binomial 所指的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Bi- two plus nomen name: a form that carries two names or two terms.
normal.cn: bi-「二」加 nomen「名字」：一个携带两个名字或两个项的形式。

normal.en: Algebra keeps the family: binomial, trinomial, monomial, polynomial.
normal.cn: 代数保留了这个词族：二项式、三项式、单项式、多项式。

normal.en: Binomial theorem, binomial coefficient and binomial distribution are fixed companions.
normal.cn: 二项式定理、二项式系数、二项分布是固定搭配。

normal.en: In biology the two parts are genus and species, written side by side.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，两部分是属名与种名，并排书写。

normal.en: The same word covers a sum and a name, because both come in twos.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指和式也指名称，因为两者都以「二」为结构。

abstract.en: Picture a sign with two halves that only read correctly when joined.
abstract.cn: 想象一块牌子分成两半，只有拼起来才读得通。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of boots: useless alone, a unit together.
abstract.cn: 想象一双靴子：单只没用，成对才是一个单位。

abstract.en: Picture a two-panel window that frames one view.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇双格窗，两格框住同一片景。

examples.en: The tutor asked the class to square the binomial without expanding every term.
examples.cn: 导师让全班在不逐项展开的情况下求这个二项式的平方。

examples.en: Each newly described beetle received a binomial in the museum register.
examples.cn: 每只新描述的甲虫都在博物馆登记册里获得一个双名。

examples.en: The binomial test is appropriate when every trial has only two outcomes.
examples.cn: 当每次试验只有两种结果时，适合使用二项检验。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one frame: two elements joined into one unit, whether the elements are algebraic terms, name parts, outcomes or words.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用同一个框架：两个要素合成一个单位，无论这两个要素是代数项、名称部分、结果还是词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single label built from two halves, neither of which is complete alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个由两半构成的标签，任何一半单独都不完整。

branches.en: ALGEBRAIC OBJECT: two terms joined by a sign form one expression that can be handled as a unit.
branches.cn: 代数对象：两个项由符号连接成一个可按单位处理的表达式。

branches.en: NAME LABEL: genus plus species, or the ink on a specimen card, is one name in two parts.
branches.cn: 名称标签：属名加种名，或标本卡上的墨迹，都是分作两部分的同一个名称。

branches.en: COUNTING PROPERTY: the adjective simply says that exactly two parts are present.
branches.cn: 数量属性：形容词只是说明恰好存在两个部分。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: statistics applies the two-part frame to success and failure.
branches.cn: 两种结果：统计学把两部分框架用在成功与失败上。

branches.en: PAIRED STRUCTURE: any two-element pairing or two-word label can borrow the word.
branches.cn: 成对结构：任何双要素配对或双词标签都可借用这个词。

intro.en: Binomial is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin noun, and both parts recur in other English words, so the word can be read as two morphemes.
intro.cn: binomial 由一个拉丁前缀和一个拉丁名词构成，两部分都重现于其他英语词，因此可按两个语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis and bini give bi- and binary; Latin nomen gives nominal, nominate, misnomer and nomenclature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bis 与 bini 给出 bi- 与 binary；拉丁 nomen 给出 nominal、nominate、misnomer 与 nomenclature。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在许多英语词中标出数量二。

items.example: Nomen is the source of several words about naming.

items.example: A trinomial has one more term than a binomial.
items.exampleCN: 三项式比二项式多一个项。

definition_en: to make amends for a wrong or injury
core_image: 把打翻的油一瓶瓶补回去，直到秤平为止
scene: 老人每周末都去河岸捡垃圾，替年轻时倾倒废料的工厂赎一份迟到的债。 He worked by the river for years to atone for his old mistakes.
sceneCN: 这里 atone 是「赎罪、弥补」（第 1 个义项：为过错作出补偿）；句意为他在河边劳作多年以弥补从前的过错。

pos.zh: 赎罪；弥补（常与 for 连用）
补偿；抵赎

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「赎罪；补偿」
由动词加人后缀构成，义为「赎罪者」

senses.title: To make amends for wrongdoing
senses.definition: to do something good as payment for a wrong
senses.definitionCN: 以善行偿还所犯的过错
senses.example: She atoned for the betrayal with years of loyal service.
senses.exampleCN: 她以多年的忠诚服务弥补那次背叛。
senses.why: At one means set at one: wrong splits people, amends reunite them.
senses.whyCN: at one 意为「合而为一」：过错使人分裂，弥补使人重归于好。

senses.title: To pay a penalty or price
senses.definition: to suffer or pay in return for harm done
senses.definitionCN: 为造成的伤害承受或付出代价
senses.example: The whole town atoned for one man's greed.
senses.exampleCN: 全城为一个人的贪婪付出代价。
senses.why: Restoring oneness requires balancing the scales again.
senses.whyCN: 恢复「合一」需要把失衡的天平重新摆平。

intro.en: Atone began as the phrase at one, set at one, a Middle English rendering of religious reconciliation.
intro.cn: atone 始于短语 at one（使合而为一），是中古英语对宗教性和解的表达。

items.en: An meant one; at an meant in union.
items.cn: 古英语 an 意为一；at an 意为合于一体。

items.en: At one described reconciling parties in dispute.
items.cn: 中古英语 at one 描述使争执双方和解。

items.en: The phrase fused into the verb atone, tied to theology.
items.cn: 十六世纪短语凝缩为动词 atone，与神学紧密相连。

items.en: Atonement named Christ's reconciling sacrifice.
items.cn: atonement 指基督的和解性献祭。

items.en: Secular uses now cover any making of amends.
items.cn: 如今世俗用法泛指一切补偿过失之举。

note.en: Atone is at one: the wrong tore, the payment sews.
note.cn: atone 即 at one：过错撕裂，补偿缝合。
